cards.src_text: For the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which went out early in the morning to hire labourers into his vineyard.
cards.tgt_text: Now will I sing to my wellbeloved a song of my beloved touching his vineyard. My wellbeloved hath a vineyard in a very fruitful hill:
cards.old_note: The Tanakh-vineyard-substance — Yashar'el (Israel) as Yahuah's vineyard.
cards.note: Isaiah 5:1 — *Now will I sing to my wellbeloved a song of my beloved touching his vineyard. My wellbeloved hath a vineyard in a very fruitful hill:* *For the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which went out early in the morning to hire labourers into his vineyard.* (Matthew 20:1) The householder who *went out early in the morning* to hire labourers walks into a field Isaiah had already sung about, the beloved's vineyard *in a very fruitful hill*. Isaiah calls on *men of Yahudah (Judah), judge, I pray you, betwixt me and my vineyard* (Isaiah 5:3), so the people hearing this parable knew whose vineyard it was: the house of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.prose: The householder who *went out early in the morning* to hire labourers walks into a field Isaiah had already sung about, the beloved's vineyard *in a very fruitful hill*. Isaiah calls on *men of Yahudah (Judah), judge, I pray you, betwixt me and my vineyard* (Isaiah 5:3), so the people hearing this parable knew whose vineyard it was: the house of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.member_note: Isaiah 5:1 — *Now will I sing to my wellbeloved a song of my beloved touching his vineyard. My wellbeloved hath a vineyard in a very fruitful hill:* Isaiah sings of the beloved's vineyard on a fruitful hill, the same vineyard the householder goes out to hire labourers into.

cards.src_text: For the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which went out early in the morning to hire labourers into his vineyard.
cards.tgt_text: Many pastors have destroyed my vineyard, they have trodden my portion under foot, they have made my pleasant portion a desolate wilderness.
cards.note: Jeremiah 12:10 — *Many pastors have destroyed my vineyard, they have trodden my portion under foot, they have made my pleasant portion a desolate wilderness.* *For the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which went out early in the morning to hire labourers into his vineyard.* (Matthew 20:1) The householder has to go out and hire because the vineyard has been ruined. Jeremiah names the ruin: *Many pastors have destroyed my vineyard*, and what they trod down was *my pleasant portion*, left a wilderness. The labourers are sent into that same vineyard, the house of Yashar'el (Israel), to work what its own shepherds laid waste.
cards.prose: The householder has to go out and hire because the vineyard has been ruined. Jeremiah names the ruin: *Many pastors have destroyed my vineyard*, and what they trod down was *my pleasant portion*, left a wilderness. The labourers are sent into that same vineyard, the house of Yashar'el (Israel), to work what its own shepherds laid waste.
cards.member_note: Jeremiah 12:10 — *Many pastors have destroyed my vineyard, they have trodden my portion under foot, they have made my pleasant portion a desolate wilderness.* Jeremiah says the shepherds destroyed the vineyard of Yahuah (the LORD) and made his pleasant portion a wilderness, the field the householder hires into.

cards.src_text: But he answered one of them, and said, Friend, I do you no wrong: did not you agree with me for a penny?
cards.tgt_text: The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.
cards.note: Matthew 6:22 — *The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.* *But he answered one of them, and said, Friend, I do you no wrong: did not you agree with me for a penny?* (Matthew 20:13) The householder answers the murmuring labourer, *Friend, I do thee no wrong*, and two verses later asks *Is thine eye evil, because I am good?* (Matthew 20:15). The eye in Matthew 6:22 is that same eye: when *thine eye be single*, the whole body is full of light, and the evil eye is the one that begrudges what the master chose to give.

cards.src_text: But he answered one of them, and said, Friend, I do you no wrong: did not you agree with me for a penny?
cards.tgt_text: Beware that there be not a thought in thy wicked heart, saying, The seventh year, the year of release, is at hand; and thine eye be evil against thy poor brother, and thou givest him nought; and he cry unto Yahuah (LORD) against thee, and it be sin unto thee.
cards.old_note: *Thine eye be evil against thy poor brother.*
cards.note: Deuteronomy 15:9 — *Beware that there be not a thought in thy wicked heart, saying, The seventh year, the year of release, is at hand; and thine eye be evil against thy poor brother, and thou givest him nought; and he cry unto Yahuah (LORD) against thee, and it be sin unto thee.* *But he answered one of them, and said, Friend, I do you no wrong: did not you agree with me for a penny?* (Matthew 20:13) The householder's question about an evil eye was not new. Moses had already named it, *thine eye be evil against thy poor brother*, and counted the withholding as sin. The labourers hired at dawn look at the men hired last, who had stood idle because *no man hath hired us* (Matthew 20:7), and begrudge them the penny the master chose to give.

The labourers hired at dawn look at the men hired last, who had stood idle because *no man hath hired us* (Matthew 20:7), and begrudge them the penny the master chose to give.
cards.member_note: Deuteronomy 15:9 — *thine eye be evil against thy poor brother, and thou givest him nought.* Moses calls the eye that begrudges a poor brother evil and counts the withholding as sin before Yahuah (the LORD).

cards.src_text: But he answered one of them, and said, Friend, I do you no wrong: did not you agree with me for a penny?
cards.tgt_text: Eat thou not the bread of him that hath an evil eye, neither desire thou his dainty meats:
cards.old_note: *Eat thou not the bread of him that hath an evil eye.*
cards.note: Proverbs 23:6 — *Eat thou not the bread of him that hath an evil eye, neither desire thou his dainty meats:* *But he answered one of them, and said, Friend, I do you no wrong: did not you agree with me for a penny?* (Matthew 20:13) Proverbs counts the evil eye as a grudging heart behind a generous-looking table: *his heart is not with thee* (Proverbs 23:7). The labourer who murmurs at the penny given to the last hired has the same eye, grudging the goodness of the one who hired him, and *an evil eye* is the name the householder gives it.

cards.src_text: But he answered one of them, and said, Friend, I do you no wrong: did not you agree with me for a penny?
cards.tgt_text: He that hasteth to be rich hath an evil eye, and considereth not that poverty shall come upon him.
cards.old_note: *He that hasteth to be rich hath an evil eye.*
cards.note: Proverbs 28:22 — *He that hasteth to be rich hath an evil eye, and considereth not that poverty shall come upon him.* *But he answered one of them, and said, Friend, I do you no wrong: did not you agree with me for a penny?* (Matthew 20:13) The men hired first had worked the whole day, and when the penny came out equal they began to measure what the others got against what they had earned. Proverbs names that grasping look: *He that hasteth to be rich hath an evil eye*. The householder's question puts the same name on it.

cards.src_text: So the last shall be first, and the first last: for many be called, but few chosen.
cards.tgt_text: But many that are first shall be last; and the last shall be first.
cards.note: Matthew 19:30 — *But many that are first shall be last; and the last shall be first.* *So the last shall be first, and the first last: for many be called, but few chosen.* (Matthew 20:16) The parable closes by saying it again, *the last shall be first, and the first last*, and the saying first came as the answer to the twelve about their seats. Just before it they had been promised thrones *judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Matthew 19:28), so the vineyard is the picture the saying needed.

cards.src_text: So the last shall be first, and the first last: for many be called, but few chosen.
cards.tgt_text: For many are called, but few are chosen.
cards.old_note: *Many are called, but few are chosen* — the wedding-feast restatement.
cards.note: Matthew 22:14 — *For many are called, but few are chosen.* *So the last shall be first, and the first last: for many be called, but few chosen.* (Matthew 20:16) Matthew 22:14 is the same sentence set at the wedding feast, *many are called, but few are chosen*, and there it follows a man who was inside the hall and was asked *how camest thou in hither not having a wedding garment?* (Matthew 22:12). Being called brings a man to the door, and what he is when the master looks at him is another matter.

cards.member_note: Matthew 22:14 — *For many are called, but few are chosen.* The sentence returns at the end of the wedding feast, spoken after a guest is found in the hall without a wedding garment.

cards.src_text: So the last shall be first, and the first last: for many be called, but few chosen.
cards.tgt_text: And he said, Go, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not.
cards.old_note: The cause-and-effect-of-hearing Tanakh-substance per Red Line #11.
cards.note: Isaiah 6:9 — *And he said, Go, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not.* *So the last shall be first, and the first last: for many be called, but few chosen.* (Matthew 20:16) Isaiah is sent to *this people* with the word *Hear ye indeed, but understand not*, and the parable ends in the same place. The call reaches many ears, and the hearing that takes hold shows who the sheep already were. Hearing does not make a sheep of anyone, which is why many are called and few chosen.
cards.prose: Isaiah is sent to *this people* with the word *Hear ye indeed, but understand not*, and the parable ends in the same place. The call reaches many ears, and the hearing that takes hold shows who the sheep already were. Hearing does not make a sheep of anyone, which is why many are called and few chosen.
cards.member_note: Isaiah 6:9 — *And he said, Go, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not.* Isaiah is sent to a people who hear without understanding, so the call reaching many ears is not the same as many being chosen.

cards.src_text: So the last shall be first, and the first last: for many be called, but few chosen.
cards.tgt_text: These shall make war with the Lamb, and the Lamb shall overcome them: for he is Lord of lords, and King of kings: and they that are with him are called, and chosen, and faithful.
cards.note: Revelation 17:14 — *These shall make war with the Lamb, and the Lamb shall overcome them: for he is Lord of lords, and King of kings: and they that are with him are called, and chosen, and faithful.* *So the last shall be first, and the first last: for many be called, but few chosen.* (Matthew 20:16) Revelation says of the ones with the Lamb that they are *called, and chosen, and faithful*, three things said together of the same people. Matthew 20:16 says many are called and few chosen, and here the few are found standing with the Lamb when war is made on him and he overcomes.

cards.src_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) going up to Jerusalem took the twelve disciples apart in the way, and said unto them,
cards.tgt_text: From that time forth began Yahusha (Jesus) to shew unto his disciples, how that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day.
cards.note: Matthew 16:21 — *From that time forth began Yahusha (Jesus) to shew unto his disciples, how that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day.* *And Yahusha (Jesus) going up to Jerusalem took the twelve disciples apart in the way, and said unto them,* (Matthew 20:17) Matthew 16:21 is where Yahusha (Jesus) first began to show his disciples that he *must go unto Jerusalem* and *suffer many things* from the elders, chief priests and scribes. In 20:17 he is on the road at last, *going up to Jerusalem*, and he takes the twelve apart to tell them again.
cards.prose: Matthew 16:21 is where Yahusha (Jesus) first began to show his disciples that he *must go unto Jerusalem* and *suffer many things* from the elders, chief priests and scribes. In 20:17 he is on the road at last, *going up to Jerusalem*, and he takes the twelve apart to tell them again.
cards.member_note: Matthew 16:21 — *he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes.* The first telling names Jerusalem and the elders, chief priests and scribes at whose hands he would be killed.

cards.src_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) going up to Jerusalem took the twelve disciples apart in the way, and said unto them,
cards.tgt_text: And while they abode in Galilee, Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, The Son of Adam shall be betrayed into the hands of men:
cards.note: Matthew 17:22 — *And while they abode in Galilee, Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, The Son of Adam shall be betrayed into the hands of men:* *And Yahusha (Jesus) going up to Jerusalem took the twelve disciples apart in the way, and said unto them,* (Matthew 20:17) The second telling came in Galilee, that the Son of Adam *shall be betrayed*, and *they were exceeding sorry* (Matthew 17:23). On the road to Jerusalem he takes the twelve apart a third time, and now the betrayal has a place and names: the chief priests and the scribes.

cards.src_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) going up to Jerusalem took the twelve disciples apart in the way, and said unto them,
cards.tgt_text: Who hath believed our report? and to whom is the arm of Yahuah (LORD) revealed?

cards.src_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) going up to Jerusalem took the twelve disciples apart in the way, and said unto them,
cards.tgt_text: My Elohim (God), my Elohim (God), why hast thou forsaken me? why art thou so far from helping me, and from the words of my roaring?
cards.note: Psalm 22:1 — *My Elohim (God), my Elohim (God), why hast thou forsaken me? why art thou so far from helping me, and from the words of my roaring?* *And Yahusha (Jesus) going up to Jerusalem took the twelve disciples apart in the way, and said unto them,* (Matthew 20:17) The road up to Jerusalem leads to the cry of Psalm 22, *why hast thou forsaken me?* It is a cry to Elohim (God) from one who still calls him *my Elohim (God)*, and the psalm goes on to remember that *Our fathers trusted in thee: they trusted, and thou didst deliver them* (Psalm 22:4).
cards.prose: The road up to Jerusalem leads to the cry of Psalm 22, *why hast thou forsaken me?* It is a cry to Elohim (God) from one who still calls him *my Elohim (God)*, and the psalm goes on to remember that *Our fathers trusted in thee: they trusted, and thou didst deliver them* (Psalm 22:4).
cards.member_note: Psalm 22:1 — *why hast thou forsaken me? why art thou so far from helping me.* The psalm opens with the cry of one brought low who still calls on his Elohim (God), the cry that waits at the end of this road.

cards.src_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) going up to Jerusalem took the twelve disciples apart in the way, and said unto them,
cards.tgt_text: And after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself: and the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary; and the end thereof shall be with a flood, and unto the end of the war desolations are determined.

cards.note: Daniel 9:26 — *And after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself: and the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary; and the end thereof shall be with a flood, and unto the end of the war desolations are determined.* *And Yahusha (Jesus) going up to Jerusalem took the twelve disciples apart in the way, and said unto them,* (Matthew 20:17) Daniel says that after *threescore and two weeks* *shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself*, and that the city and the sanctuary are destroyed after it. Yahusha (Jesus) is on the road to that city, telling the twelve he will be condemned there, so the cutting off Daniel names is the one he is walking toward.

cards.src_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) going up to Jerusalem took the twelve disciples apart in the way, and said unto them,
cards.tgt_text: And I will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplications: and they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son, and shall be in bitterness for him, as one that is in bitterness for his firstborn.
cards.note: Zechariah 12:10 — *And I will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplications: and they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son, and shall be in bitterness for him, as one that is in bitterness for his firstborn.* *And Yahusha (Jesus) going up to Jerusalem took the twelve disciples apart in the way, and said unto them,* (Matthew 20:17) Yahuah (the LORD) says through Zechariah that he will pour out *the spirit of grace and of supplications*, and *they shall look upon me whom they have pierced*, and mourn *as one mourneth for his only son*. The one going up to Jerusalem to be handed over and crucified is the one they will look on, and the looking is for the house of David and the people of that city.

cards.src_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) going up to Jerusalem took the twelve disciples apart in the way, and said unto them,
cards.tgt_text: Awake, O sword, against my shepherd, and against the man that is my fellow, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts): smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered: and I will turn mine hand upon the little ones.
cards.note: Zechariah 13:7 — *Awake, O sword, against my shepherd, and against the man that is my fellow, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts): smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered: and I will turn mine hand upon the little ones.* *And Yahusha (Jesus) going up to Jerusalem took the twelve disciples apart in the way, and said unto them,* (Matthew 20:17) Yahuah (the LORD) calls the sword against *my shepherd, and against the man that is my fellow*, and *the sheep shall be scattered*. Yahusha (Jesus) takes the twelve apart to tell them the shepherd will be struck, and Zechariah goes on to a third brought through the fire until they say *It is my people* (Zechariah 13:9).
cards.prose: Yahuah (the LORD) calls the sword against *my shepherd, and against the man that is my fellow*, and *the sheep shall be scattered*. Yahusha (Jesus) takes the twelve apart to tell them the shepherd will be struck, and Zechariah goes on to a third brought through the fire until they say *It is my people* (Zechariah 13:9).
cards.member_note: Zechariah 13:7 — *smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered.* Zechariah calls the sword against the shepherd who is Yahuah's (the LORD's) fellow, and the sheep are scattered, with a third left to be refined.

cards.src_text: Then came to him the mother of Zebedee’s children with her sons, worshipping him, and desiring a certain thing of him.
cards.tgt_text: And going on from thence, he saw other two brethren, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in a ship with Zebedee their father, mending their nets; and he called them.
cards.old_note: The calling of Ya'aqov (James) and Yochanan (John).
cards.note: Matthew 4:21 — *And going on from thence, he saw other two brethren, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in a ship with Zebedee their father, mending their nets; and he called them.* *Then came to him the mother of Zebedee’s children with her sons, worshipping him, and desiring a certain thing of him.* (Matthew 20:20) James and John were mending nets with their father Zebedee when he called them, and they *immediately left the ship and their father* (Matthew 4:22) and followed him. Now their mother comes *with her sons* to ask for places beside him, so the two who left everything are the two for whom the highest seats are asked.
cards.prose: James and John were mending nets with their father Zebedee when he called them, and they *immediately left the ship and their father* (Matthew 4:22) and followed him. Now their mother comes *with her sons* to ask for places beside him, so the two who left everything are the two for whom the highest seats are asked.
cards.member_note: Matthew 4:21 — *he saw other two brethren, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother.* Matthew 4:21 shows James and John called from their father's ship, the two whose mother now asks the highest places for them.

cards.src_text: Then came to him the mother of Zebedee’s children with her sons, worshipping him, and desiring a certain thing of him.
cards.tgt_text: And after six days Yahusha (Jesus) taketh Peter, James, and John his brother, and bringeth them up into an high mountain apart,
cards.note: Matthew 17:1 — *And after six days Yahusha (Jesus) taketh Peter, James, and John his brother, and bringeth them up into an high mountain apart,* *Then came to him the mother of Zebedee’s children with her sons, worshipping him, and desiring a certain thing of him.* (Matthew 20:20) James and John were among the three Yahusha (Jesus) took *up into an high mountain apart*, where Moses and Elijah talked with him. Their mother's request, *the one on thy right hand, and the other on the left* (Matthew 20:21), asks that the nearness they had on that mountain be kept in his kingdom.
cards.prose: James and John were among the three Yahusha (Jesus) took *up into an high mountain apart*, where Moses and Elijah talked with him. Their mother's request, *the one on thy right hand, and the other on the left* (Matthew 20:21), asks that the nearness they had on that mountain be kept in his kingdom.

cards.src_text: Then came to him the mother of Zebedee’s children with her sons, worshipping him, and desiring a certain thing of him.
cards.tgt_text: And James and John, the sons of Zebedee, come unto him, saying, Master, we would that thou shouldest do for us whatsoever we shall desire.
cards.note: Mark 10:35 — *And James and John, the sons of Zebedee, come unto him, saying, Master, we would that thou shouldest do for us whatsoever we shall desire.* *Then came to him the mother of Zebedee’s children with her sons, worshipping him, and desiring a certain thing of him.* (Matthew 20:20) In Mark the sons speak for themselves, asking that he *do for us whatsoever we shall desire*, where Matthew has their mother bring them. Whoever voices it, the answer is the same in both: *Ye know not what ye ask* (Mark 10:38).

cards.src_text: Even as the Son of Adam came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.
cards.tgt_text: If there be laid on him a sum of money, then he shall give for the ransom of his life whatsoever is laid upon him.

When Yahusha (Jesus) says the Son of Adam came *to give his life a ransom for many*, he uses the Torah's own word, and this time the price is the life of the one who gives it.

cards.tgt_text: And Yahuah (LORD) spake unto Moses, saying,
cards.note: Exodus 30:11 — *And Yahuah (LORD) spake unto Moses, saying,* *Even as the Son of Adam came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.* (Matthew 20:28) Yahuah (the LORD) speaks to Moses and sets a ransom on every numbered soul: *then shall they give every man a ransom for his soul unto Yahuah (LORD)* (Exodus 30:12), paid as *half a shekel after the shekel of the sanctuary* (Exodus 30:13). cards.tgt_text: And David said on that day, Whosoever getteth up to the gutter, and smiteth the Jebusites, and the lame and the blind, that are hated of David’s soul, he shall be chief and captain. Wherefore they said, The blind and the lame shall not come into the house.
cards.note: 2 Samuel 5:8 — *And David said on that day, Whosoever getteth up to the gutter, and smiteth the Jebusites, and the lame and the blind, that are hated of David’s soul, he shall be chief and captain. Wherefore they said, The blind and the lame shall not come into the house.* *And the blind and the lame came to him in the temple; and he healed them.* (Matthew 21:14) The words *The blind and the lame shall not come into the house* come out of David's taking of Zion, where the Jebusites had boasted *Except thou take away the blind and the lame, thou shalt not come in hither* (2 Samuel 5:6). A certain man had two sons; and he came to the first, and said, Son, go work to day in my vineyard.* (Matthew 21:28) In the parable the father's word is *go work to day in my vineyard*, and in the Sermon the question is who does *the will of my Father which is in heaven*. The second son says yes and does not go, which is the *Adonai (Lord), Adonai (Lord)* kind of yes that gets no entry. It is the doing that is counted.

A certain man had two sons; and he came to the first, and said, Son, go work to day in my vineyard.* (Matthew 21:28) The people of Ezekiel's day talked about the prophet at their walls and doors and told each other *Come, I pray you, and hear what is the word*. cards.tgt_text: But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.
cards.old_note: *Be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only.*
cards.note: James 1:22 — *But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.* *But what think you? The husbandmen are the ones put in charge of it, not the vineyard.

cards.tgt_text: And there was also a man that prophesied in the name of Yahuah (LORD), Urijah the son of Shemaiah of Kirjath-jearim, who prophesied against this city and against this land according to all the words of Jeremiah:

cards.src_text: And whosoever shall fall on this stone shall be broken: but on whomsoever it shall fall, it will grind him to powder.
cards.tgt_text: Thou sawest till that a stone was cut out without hands, which smote the image upon his feet that were of iron and clay, and brake them to pieces.
cards.note: Daniel 2:34 — *Thou sawest till that a stone was cut out without hands, which smote the image upon his feet that were of iron and clay, and brake them to pieces.* *And whosoever shall fall on this stone shall be broken: but on whomsoever it shall fall, it will grind him to powder.* (Matthew 21:44) *It will grind him to powder* is where Daniel's stone ends too. It strikes the image on its feet, and the iron, the clay, the brass, the silver and the gold *became like the chaff of the summer threshingfloors* (Daniel 2:35), carried off by the wind. In Daniel the stone falls on kingdoms and breaks them, and in Matthew it falls on whoever stumbles against it.

cards.note: Isaiah 25:6 — *And in this mountain shall Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) make unto all people a feast of fat things, a feast of wines on the lees, of fat things full of marrow, of wines on the lees well refined.* *And Yahusha (Jesus) answered and spake unto them again by parables, and said,* (Matthew 22:1) The parable he is about to tell is a feast, and Isaiah had already set the table: *a feast of fat things* on the mountain of Yahuah (the LORD). cards.tgt_text: If brethren dwell together, and one of them die, and have no child, the wife of the dead shall not marry without unto a stranger: her husband’s brother shall go in unto her, and take her to him to wife, and perform the duty of an husband’s brother unto her.
cards.note: Deuteronomy 25:5 — *If brethren dwell together, and one of them die, and have no child, the wife of the dead shall not marry without unto a stranger: her husband’s brother shall go in unto her, and take her to him to wife, and perform the duty of an husband’s brother unto her.* *The same day came to him the Sadducees, which say that there is no resurrection, and asked him,* (Matthew 22:23) The riddle is built on a commandment of Moses: when a brother dies without a child, his brother *shall go in unto her* and carry the dead man's name forward. The law is Moses', and the Sadducees take it and set it against the resurrection, as if a duty to a dead man's line could make the dead rising look absurd.

cards.src_text: The same day came to him the Sadducees, which say that there is no resurrection, and asked him,
cards.tgt_text: And it came to pass at that time, that Yahudah (Judah) went down from his brethren, and turned in to a certain Adullamite, whose name was Hirah.

The seed was carried forward by the brother, which is what the seven brothers in the riddle are supposed to be doing.

cards.old_note: *To do justly, and to love mercy.*

Loving Yahuah (the LORD) and loving the neighbour is that walk laid out, and the prophets say it as plainly as the law does.

cards.src_text: Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, You shall love Yahuah Elohayka (the Lord thy God) with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind.
cards.tgt_text: For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of Elohim (God) more than burnt offerings.

He is turning from sacrifice with no knowing of him behind it, and the knowing shows in how a man deals with his neighbour.

cards.src_text: On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.
cards.tgt_text: Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets.
cards.old_note: The Golden Rule + *for this is the law and the prophets.*
cards.note: Matthew 7:12 — *Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets.* *On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.* (Matthew 22:40) He said it at the close of the Sermon on the Mount and he says it again to the lawyer: all that you would have men do to you, do to them, *for this is the law and the prophets*. Twice the law and the prophets are said to rest on how a man treats his neighbour, and neither time are they taken away.

cards.src_text: On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.
cards.tgt_text: Owe no man any thing, but to love one another: for he that loveth another hath fulfilled the law.
cards.old_note: *Love is the fulfilling of the law.*
cards.note: Romans 13:8 — *Owe no man any thing, but to love one another: for he that loveth another hath fulfilled the law.* *On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.* (Matthew 22:40) Paul says it too: *he that loveth another hath fulfilled the law*, and the next verse names the commandments love keeps, *Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shalt not kill, Thou shalt not steal* (Romans 13:9). Love does not stand in for the law, and it is how the commandments get done.

cards.src_text: On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.
cards.tgt_text: For all the law is fulfilled in one word, even in this; Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.
cards.old_note: *All the law is fulfilled in one word.*

The whole law is still standing there to be fulfilled, and the sentence would say nothing if it were gone.

cards.src_text: On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.
cards.tgt_text: If ye fulfil the royal law according to the scripture, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself, ye do well:

He says those who fulfil it *do well*, and in the next lines he goes on to the commandments against adultery and killing, so the law is still named and still being kept.

cards.src_text: On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.
cards.tgt_text: There cometh a woman of Samaria to draw water: Yahusha (Jesus) saith unto her, Give me to drink.
cards.note: John 4:7 — *There cometh a woman of Samaria to draw water: Yahusha (Jesus) saith unto her, Give me to drink.* *On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.* (Matthew 22:40) At Jacob's well, wearied from the road, Yahusha (Jesus) asks a woman of Samaria for a drink, on the ground Jacob gave to his son Joseph. The second commandment is walked out there: he goes to one the Yahudim (Jews) had no dealings with and asks her for something, as a neighbour would.

cards.src_text: On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.

cards.src_text: While the Pharisees were gathered together, Yahusha (Jesus) asked them,
cards.tgt_text: Yahuah (LORD) said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.

cards.src_text: While the Pharisees were gathered together, Yahusha (Jesus) asked them,
cards.tgt_text: Yahuah (LORD) hath sworn, and will not repent, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melek Tsadiq (Melchizedek).

cards.src_text: While the Pharisees were gathered together, Yahusha (Jesus) asked them,
cards.tgt_text: I will declare the decree: Yahuah (LORD) hath said unto me, Thou art my Son; this day have I begotten thee.

cards.src_text: While the Pharisees were gathered together, Yahusha (Jesus) asked them,
cards.tgt_text: And when thy days be fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom.

cards.src_text: While the Pharisees were gathered together, Yahusha (Jesus) asked them,

cards.src_text: While the Pharisees were gathered together, Yahusha (Jesus) asked them,
cards.tgt_text: I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.

cards.note: Daniel 7:13 — *I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.* *While the Pharisees were gathered together, Yahusha (Jesus) asked them,* (Matthew 22:41) The one David bows to sits at the right hand in the psalm, and in Daniel *one like the Son of Adam* comes with the clouds to the Ancient of days and is given a kingdom that *shall not pass away* (Daniel 7:14). cards.src_text: While the Pharisees were gathered together, Yahusha (Jesus) asked them,

cards.tgt_text: But to which of the angels said he at any time, Sit on my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool?
cards.note: Hebrews 1:13 — *But to which of the angels said he at any time, Sit on my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool?* *While the Pharisees were gathered together, Yahusha (Jesus) asked them,* (Matthew 22:41) The psalm is put to the angels as a question, and the answer is none. Elohim (God) said *Sit on my right hand* to one only, the Son named in the verses just before, so the one David bows to is no angel and no mere son of David, but the one the Father seats.

cards.member_note: Hebrews 1:13 — *But to which of the angels said he at any time, Sit on my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool?* Hebrews asks which angel was ever told to sit at the right hand, so the one David bows to is no angel.

cards.src_text: Saying, The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat:
cards.tgt_text: If there arise a matter too hard for thee in judgment, between blood and blood, between plea and plea, and between stroke and stroke, being matters of controversy within thy gates: then shalt thou arise, and get thee up into the place which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) shall choose;
cards.note: Deuteronomy 17:8 — *If there arise a matter too hard for thee in judgment, between blood and blood, between plea and plea, and between stroke and stroke, being matters of controversy within thy gates: then shalt thou arise, and get thee up into the place which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) shall choose;* *Saying, The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat:* (Matthew 23:2) Moses' seat was not invented by the Pharisees. Here a case too hard for the local judges goes up to the priests and the judge, and a verse later the sentence to be done is *according to the sentence of the law which they shall teach thee* (Deuteronomy 17:11). That is why Yahusha (Jesus) can say to observe what they bid: what is read from the seat is Moses, and the fault lies in their works.

cards.src_text: Saying, The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat:
cards.tgt_text: For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts).
cards.note: Malachi 2:7 — *For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts).* *Saying, The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat:* (Matthew 23:2) Malachi says what the seat is for. The priest's lips *should keep knowledge*, and the people *seek the law at his mouth*, since the priest stands as a messenger for Yahuah (the LORD) of hosts. The next verse turns on priests who *caused many to stumble at the law* (Malachi 2:8), the same line Yahusha (Jesus) draws between the law read from the seat and the works of the men sitting in it.

cards.src_text: For they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers.
cards.tgt_text: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
cards.old_note: *My yoke is easy, and my burden is light.* The contrast.
cards.note: Matthew 11:28 — *Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.* *For they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers.* (Matthew 23:4) The heavy burdens in this verse are the weight men stacked up and would not touch themselves, and here Yahusha (Jesus) calls the ones who are *heavy laden* to come to him for rest. What he lifts is what was laid on top, and a few verses on he says of his own yoke, *my yoke is easy, and my burden is light* (Matthew 11:30).

cards.src_text: For they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers.
cards.tgt_text: Now therefore why tempt ye Elohim (God), to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?
cards.old_note: *A yoke ... which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear.* The apostolic-restatement.
cards.note: Acts 15:10 — *Now therefore why tempt ye Elohim (God), to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?* *For they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers.* (Matthew 23:4) Peter's *yoke* is what the seat laid on shoulders, a price at the door: *Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved* (Acts 15:1). He does not call the Torah unbearable, since the Torah is what the fathers lived by and what is read from the seat. He means the rule that nobody is in until the rite is done.

cards.member_note: Acts 15:10 — *to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear.* Peter says the yoke put on the disciples' necks was one that neither the fathers nor the apostles were able to bear.

cards.src_text: But all their works they do for to be seen of men: they make broad their phylacteries, and enlarge the borders of their garments,
cards.tgt_text: And it shall be for a sign unto thee upon thine hand, and for a memorial between thine eyes, that the LORD’S law may be in thy mouth: for with a strong hand hath Yahuah (LORD) brought thee out of Egypt.
cards.note: Exodus 13:9 — *And it shall be for a sign unto thee upon thine hand, and for a memorial between thine eyes, that the LORD’S law may be in thy mouth: for with a strong hand hath Yahuah (LORD) brought thee out of Egypt.* *But all their works they do for to be seen of men: they make broad their phylacteries, and enlarge the borders of their garments,* (Matthew 23:5) The sign on the hand and the memorial between the eyes are commanded, *that the LORD’S law may be in thy mouth*. Yahusha (Jesus) does not say to leave them off. What he marks is that they *make broad their phylacteries* to be seen, which turns something meant to keep the law in the mouth into something to be looked at.

cards.src_text: But all their works they do for to be seen of men: they make broad their phylacteries, and enlarge the borders of their garments,
cards.tgt_text: And it shall be for a token upon thine hand, and for frontlets between thine eyes: for by strength of hand Yahuah (LORD) brought us forth out of Egypt.
cards.note: Exodus 13:16 — *And it shall be for a token upon thine hand, and for frontlets between thine eyes: for by strength of hand Yahuah (LORD) brought us forth out of Egypt.* *But all their works they do for to be seen of men: they make broad their phylacteries, and enlarge the borders of their garments,* (Matthew 23:5) Exodus says it twice, here as *a token upon thine hand, and for frontlets between thine eyes*, and each time the reason is the same, that Yahuah (the LORD) brought them out of Egypt. It is a reminder of what he did. When the Pharisees make theirs broad to be noticed, they turn a remembrance into a show, and the show is what Yahusha (Jesus) names.

cards.src_text: But all their works they do for to be seen of men: they make broad their phylacteries, and enlarge the borders of their garments,
cards.tgt_text: Speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and bid them that they make them fringes in the borders of their garments throughout their generations, and that they put upon the fringe of the borders a ribband of blue:
cards.note: Numbers 15:38 — *Speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and bid them that they make them fringes in the borders of their garments throughout their generations, and that they put upon the fringe of the borders a ribband of blue:* *But all their works they do for to be seen of men: they make broad their phylacteries, and enlarge the borders of their garments,* (Matthew 23:5) The border is a commandment too: *make them fringes in the borders of their garments*, throughout their generations, with a ribband of blue. Yahusha (Jesus) wore one himself, so the fault he names is the habit of the Pharisees to *enlarge the borders* to be seen, and not the fringe.

cards.src_text: But all their works they do for to be seen of men: they make broad their phylacteries, and enlarge the borders of their garments,
cards.tgt_text: Thou shalt make thee fringes upon the four quarters of thy vesture, wherewith thou coverest thyself.
cards.note: Deuteronomy 22:12 — *Thou shalt make thee fringes upon the four quarters of thy vesture, wherewith thou coverest thyself.* *But all their works they do for to be seen of men: they make broad their phylacteries, and enlarge the borders of their garments,* (Matthew 23:5) Moses puts the fringe on the garment a second time, *upon the four quarters of thy vesture*, so it is a plain commandment for everyone who wears a cloak and not a badge for a few. What Yahusha (Jesus) faults is making the border larger for men to admire, not the fringe itself.

cards.src_text: But be not you called Rabbi: for one is your Master, even Messiah (Christ); and all you are brethren.
cards.tgt_text: Doubtless thou art our father, though Abraham be ignorant of us, and Yashar'el (Israel) acknowledge us not: thou, O Yahuah (LORD), art our father, our redeemer; thy name is from everlasting.
cards.note: Isaiah 63:16 — *Doubtless thou art our father, though Abraham be ignorant of us, and Yashar'el (Israel) acknowledge us not: thou, O Yahuah (LORD), art our father, our redeemer; thy name is from everlasting.* *But be not you called Rabbi: for one is your Master, even Messiah (Christ); and all you are brethren.* (Matthew 23:8) Isaiah's people say it when even the fathers cannot help them: *though Abraham be ignorant of us*, still *thou, O Yahuah (LORD), art our father*. That stands behind what Yahusha (Jesus) says to the crowd, one Master and all of them brothers, and in the very next verse one Father in heaven.

That stands behind what Yahusha (Jesus) says to the crowd, one Master and all of them brothers, and in the very next verse one Father in heaven.
cards.member_note: Isaiah 63:16 — *thou, O Yahuah (LORD), art our father, our redeemer.* Even if Abraham does not know them, the people say Yahuah (the LORD) is their father and their redeemer, so the Father alone is Father.

cards.src_text: But be not you called Rabbi: for one is your Master, even Messiah (Christ); and all you are brethren.
cards.tgt_text: But now, O Yahuah (LORD), thou art our father; we are the clay, and thou our potter; and we all are the work of thy hand.
cards.note: Isaiah 64:8 — *But now, O Yahuah (LORD), thou art our father; we are the clay, and thou our potter; and we all are the work of thy hand.* *But be not you called Rabbi: for one is your Master, even Messiah (Christ); and all you are brethren.* (Matthew 23:8) *We are the clay, and thou our potter*, Isaiah says, and *we all are the work of thy hand*. Everyone made by the one hand stands level, which is why Yahusha (Jesus) can say *all ye are brethren* and leave only one Master over them.
cards.prose: *We are the clay, and thou our potter*, Isaiah says, and *we all are the work of thy hand*. Everyone made by the one hand stands level, which is why Yahusha (Jesus) can say *all ye are brethren* and leave only one Master over them.
cards.member_note: Isaiah 64:8 — *But now, O Yahuah (LORD), thou art our father; we are the clay, and thou our potter; and we all are the work of thy hand.* The people are the clay and Yahuah (the LORD) is the potter, so all are the work of one hand and none stands over the rest as father.

cards.src_text: But be not you called Rabbi: for one is your Master, even Messiah (Christ); and all you are brethren.
cards.tgt_text: Do ye thus requite Yahuah (LORD), O foolish people and unwise? is not he thy father that hath bought thee? hath he not made thee, and established thee?
cards.note: Deuteronomy 32:6 — *Do ye thus requite Yahuah (LORD), O foolish people and unwise? is not he thy father that hath bought thee? hath he not made thee, and established thee?* *But be not you called Rabbi: for one is your Master, even Messiah (Christ); and all you are brethren.* (Matthew 23:8) *Is not he thy father that hath bought thee?* Moses asks a people that had forgotten. The one who made them and established them is called Father there, which is why Yahusha (Jesus) leaves them one Master, calls them all brethren, and names one Father in heaven.
cards.prose: *Is not he thy father that hath bought thee?* Moses asks a people that had forgotten. The one who made them and established them is called Father there, which is why Yahusha (Jesus) leaves them one Master, calls them all brethren, and names one Father in heaven.
cards.member_note: Deuteronomy 32:6 — *is not he thy father that hath bought thee? hath he not made thee, and established thee.* Moses calls Yahuah (the LORD) the father who bought, made and established the people, so fatherhood in Yashar'el (Israel) belongs to him.

cards.src_text: But be not you called Rabbi: for one is your Master, even Messiah (Christ); and all you are brethren.
cards.tgt_text: For though ye have ten thousand instructers in Messiah (Christ), yet have ye not many fathers: for in HaMashiach Yahusha (Christ Jesus) I have begotten you through the gospel.
cards.old_note: *In Messiah (Christ) Yahusha (Jesus) I have begotten you through the gospel.* The Pauline-substance — the substantial-substance-of-the-substance-of-the-substantial-substance-of-Pauline-substantial-substance-of-substantial-paternity-substance the substance the Pauline-substance walks-at-the-substantial-substance-of-the-substantial-substance-of-the-substance-of-substantial-substance the substance does-NOT-substantially-overturn the King's-substance at Matt 23:9 substance.
cards.note: 1 Corinthians 4:15 — *For though ye have ten thousand instructers in Messiah (Christ), yet have ye not many fathers: for in HaMashiach Yahusha (Christ Jesus) I have begotten you through the gospel.* *But be not you called Rabbi: for one is your Master, even Messiah (Christ); and all you are brethren.* (Matthew 23:8) Paul takes no title here. They have *ten thousand instructers*, he says, but not many fathers, and the only fatherhood he claims is that *I have begotten you through the gospel*, a bringing to birth he did among them and no rank he wears over them. That is the opposite of men loving to be called Rabbi.

cards.src_text: But he that is greatest among you shall be your servant.
cards.tgt_text: At the same time came the disciples unto Yahusha (Jesus), saying, Who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?
cards.note: Matthew 18:1 — *At the same time came the disciples unto Yahusha (Jesus), saying, Who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?* *But he that is greatest among you shall be your servant.* (Matthew 23:11) The question the seat answers with chief places is the one the disciples ask themselves here, *Who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?* Yahusha (Jesus) sets a little child in the middle: *Whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child, the same is greatest in the kingdom of heaven* (Matthew 18:4). That is the same low road as *he that is greatest among you shall be your servant*.

cards.src_text: But he that is greatest among you shall be your servant.
cards.tgt_text: But Yahusha (Jesus) called them unto him, and said, Ye know that the princes of the Gentiles exercise dominion over them, and they that are great exercise authority upon them.
cards.note: Matthew 20:25 — *But Yahusha (Jesus) called them unto him, and said, Ye know that the princes of the Gentiles exercise dominion over them, and they that are great exercise authority upon them.* *But he that is greatest among you shall be your servant.* (Matthew 23:11) Yahusha (Jesus) sets two ways of ruling side by side. The *princes of the Gentiles exercise dominion*, and then he says *But it shall not be so among you* (Matthew 20:26). The love of chief seats is the way of those princes, and the kingdom runs the other way, where the one who is greatest is the servant.

cards.src_text: But he that is greatest among you shall be your servant.
cards.tgt_text: But he giveth more grace. Wherefore he saith, Elohim (God) resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble.

It is the same turn Yahusha (Jesus) names in the next verse, *whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased; and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted* (Matthew 23:12), and James says whose hand does the turning.

cards.src_text: But he that is greatest among you shall be your servant.
cards.tgt_text: Humble yourselves in the sight of Yahuah (Lord), and he shall lift you up.
cards.old_note: *Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord.*
cards.note: James 4:10 — *Humble yourselves in the sight of Yahuah (Lord), and he shall lift you up.* *But he that is greatest among you shall be your servant.* (Matthew 23:11) James gives the other half of the servant's greatness. The lifting is not taken but given, *he shall lift you up*, and it is done in the sight of Yahuah (the LORD) and not before men watching the chief seats. The servant stays low and the one who sees him raises him.
cards.prose: James gives the other half of the servant's greatness. The lifting is not taken but given, *he shall lift you up*, and it is done in the sight of Yahuah (the LORD) and not before men watching the chief seats. The servant stays low and the one who sees him raises him.

cards.src_text: But he that is greatest among you shall be your servant.
cards.tgt_text: Likewise, ye younger, submit yourselves unto the elder. Yea, all of you be subject one to another, and be clothed with humility: for Elohim (God) resisteth the proud, and giveth grace to the humble.
cards.note: 1 Peter 5:5 — *Likewise, ye younger, submit yourselves unto the elder. Yea, all of you be subject one to another, and be clothed with humility: for Elohim (God) resisteth the proud, and giveth grace to the humble.* *But he that is greatest among you shall be your servant.* (Matthew 23:11) Peter shows the servant's rule in a house with elders and younger. The younger submit to the elder, yet *all of you be subject one to another*, and all are to be *clothed with humility*. Greatness there is wearing humility, since Elohim (God) *resisteth the proud*.
cards.prose: Peter shows the servant's rule in a house with elders and younger. The younger submit to the elder, yet *all of you be subject one to another*, and all are to be *clothed with humility*. Greatness there is wearing humility, since Elohim (God) *resisteth the proud*.
cards.member_note: 1 Peter 5:5 — *Yea, all of you be subject one to another, and be clothed with humility.* Everyone in the house is to be subject to one another and clothed with humility, because Elohim (God) resists the proud.

cards.src_text: Woe unto you, you blind guides, which say, Whosoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gold of the temple, he is a debtor!
cards.tgt_text: Again, ye have heard that it hath been said by them of old time, Thou shalt not forswear thyself, but shalt perform unto Yahuah (Lord) thine oaths:
cards.old_note: *Swear not at all.* The earlier substance.
cards.note: Matthew 5:33 — *Again, ye have heard that it hath been said by them of old time, Thou shalt not forswear thyself, but shalt perform unto Yahuah (Lord) thine oaths:* *Woe unto you, you blind guides, which say, Whosoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gold of the temple, he is a debtor!* (Matthew 23:16) Here the oath is set down first as a commandment: *shalt perform unto Yahuah (Lord) thine oaths*. That is the line the blind guides step around. A man who swears by the gold or the gift and calls the other oath *it is nothing* has found a way out of performing what he swore.

cards.src_text: Woe unto you, you blind guides, which say, Whosoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gold of the temple, he is a debtor!
cards.tgt_text: And ye shall not swear by my name falsely, neither shalt thou profane the name of thy Elohim (God): I am Yahuah (LORD).

That is why the answer to the gold and the gift traces every oath upward: *whoso shall swear by the temple, sweareth by it, and by him that dwelleth therein* (Matthew 23:21). cards.src_text: Woe unto you, you blind guides, which say, Whosoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gold of the temple, he is a debtor!
cards.tgt_text: If a man vow a vow unto Yahuah (LORD), or swear an oath to bind his soul with a bond; he shall not break his word, he shall do according to all that proceedeth out of his mouth.
cards.note: Numbers 30:2 — *If a man vow a vow unto Yahuah (LORD), or swear an oath to bind his soul with a bond; he shall not break his word, he shall do according to all that proceedeth out of his mouth.* *Woe unto you, you blind guides, which say, Whosoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gold of the temple, he is a debtor!* (Matthew 23:16) Numbers puts it without an exception: *he shall not break his word*, and he is held to *all that proceedeth out of his mouth*. A system that sorts oaths into the ones that bind and the ones where *it is nothing* has made exceptions the commandment never made.

cards.tgt_text: When thou shalt vow a vow unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), thou shalt not slack to pay it: for Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) will surely require it of thee; and it would be sin in thee.

Calling an oath by the temple *it is nothing* and one by the gold a debt only moves the debt around, because Yahuah (the LORD) *will surely require it of thee*.

cards.prose: Here is the tithe the Pharisees paid down to the herbs, and it is a commandment: *Thou shalt truly tithe*. Yahusha (Jesus) does not touch it. He says *these ought ye to have done*, and faults them only for leaving the weightier matters undone beside it.
cards.member_note: Deuteronomy 14:22 — *Thou shalt truly tithe all the increase of thy seed, that the field bringeth forth year by year.* The tithe of the increase of the field is Torah's own commandment, which the woe leaves standing.

cards.src_text: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for you pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin, and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith: these ought you to have done, and not to leave the other undone.
cards.tgt_text: And all the tithe of the land, whether of the seed of the land, or of the fruit of the tree, is the LORD’S: it is holy unto Yahuah (LORD).
cards.note: Leviticus 27:30 — *And all the tithe of the land, whether of the seed of the land, or of the fruit of the tree, is the LORD’S: it is holy unto Yahuah (LORD).* *Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for you pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin, and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith: these ought you to have done, and not to leave the other undone.* (Matthew 23:23) The tithe is called *holy unto Yahuah (LORD)*, so a man who tithes mint and anise and cummin is handling something set apart, and the woe does not ask him to stop. It asks that he not stop there, since the same Yahuah (the LORD) asks for judgment, mercy and faith. *Not to leave the other undone* means both stand together.

cards.src_text: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for you make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess.
cards.tgt_text: And he called the multitude, and said unto them, Hear, and understand:
cards.note: Matthew 15:10 — *And he called the multitude, and said unto them, Hear, and understand:* *Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for you make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess.* (Matthew 23:25) He calls the multitude to *Hear, and understand*, and what he teaches is the cup turned inside out: *that which cometh out of the mouth, this defileth a man* (Matthew 15:11). A man can scrub the *outside of the cup and of the platter* all day, and what is *within* is what he is carrying.

cards.src_text: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for you make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess.
cards.tgt_text: Then came together unto him the Pharisees, and certain of the scribes, which came from Jerusalem.
cards.old_note: The Markan-parallel of the heart-defilement substance.
cards.note: Mark 7:1 — *Then came together unto him the Pharisees, and certain of the scribes, which came from Jerusalem.* *Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for you make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess.* (Matthew 23:25) Mark opens the same fight with Pharisees and scribes who *came from Jerusalem* to find fault over unwashed hands, and a few verses on names *the washing of cups, and pots, brasen vessels* (Mark 7:4). That is the cup and platter of the woe, a tradition of cleaning the outside of vessels while the inside went unwashed.

cards.src_text: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for you are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men’s bones, and of all uncleanness.
cards.tgt_text: He that toucheth the dead body of any man shall be unclean seven days.
cards.note: Numbers 19:11 — *He that toucheth the dead body of any man shall be unclean seven days.* *Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for you are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men’s bones, and of all uncleanness.* (Matthew 23:27) This is the real uncleanness the paint covers: whoever touches the dead body *shall be unclean seven days*. Yahusha (Jesus) says the men in the seat are like whited tombs *full of dead men’s bones, and of all uncleanness*, so what looked beautiful outside is the very thing the law says defiles, and nobody walking past was warned.

cards.src_text: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for you are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men’s bones, and of all uncleanness.
cards.tgt_text: Because, even because they have seduced my people, saying, Peace; and there was no peace; and one built up a wall, and, lo, others daubed it with untempered morter:
cards.note: Ezekiel 13:10 — *Because, even because they have seduced my people, saying, Peace; and there was no peace; and one built up a wall, and, lo, others daubed it with untempered morter:* *Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for you are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men’s bones, and of all uncleanness.* (Matthew 23:27) The wall *daubed it with untempered morter* is the same trick as the whited tomb, a coat that makes something look sound over what is not. Ezekiel's prophets cried *Peace; and there was no peace*, and Yahusha (Jesus) says the tombs *appear beautiful outward*. In Ezekiel the daubed wall comes down: *that it shall fall* (Ezekiel 13:11).

cards.src_text: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because you build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous,
cards.tgt_text: Since the day that your fathers came forth out of the land of Egypt unto this day I have even sent unto you all my servants the prophets, daily rising up early and sending them:
cards.note: Jeremiah 7:25 — *Since the day that your fathers came forth out of the land of Egypt unto this day I have even sent unto you all my servants the prophets, daily rising up early and sending them:* *Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because you build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous,* (Matthew 23:29) In Jeremiah, Yahuah (the LORD) has been sending *all my servants the prophets*, *daily rising up early*, since the day the fathers left Egypt. The woe is the long end of that sending, with men now building the tombs of the prophets who were refused. The sending is the same one, and only the tombs are new.

cards.src_text: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because you build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous,
cards.tgt_text: And Yahuah (LORD) hath sent unto you all his servants the prophets, rising early and sending them; but ye have not hearkened, nor inclined your ear to hear.
cards.old_note: *Yahuah (the LORD) hath sent unto you all his servants the prophets.*
cards.note: Jeremiah 25:4 — *And Yahuah (LORD) hath sent unto you all his servants the prophets, rising early and sending them; but ye have not hearkened, nor inclined your ear to hear.* *Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because you build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous,* (Matthew 23:29) *But ye have not hearkened*, Jeremiah says of the prophets Yahuah (the LORD) sent, and Yahusha (Jesus) says the ones who *garnish the sepulchres of the righteous* were not listening either. A decorated tomb honors a prophet who is dead. The question put to Jeremiah's hearers was whether the living one was heard.

cards.src_text: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because you build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous,
cards.tgt_text: Nevertheless they were disobedient, and rebelled against thee, and cast thy law behind their backs, and slew thy prophets which testified against them to turn them to thee, and they wrought great provocations.
cards.old_note: *Slew thy prophets which testified against them.*
cards.note: Nehemiah 9:26 — *Nevertheless they were disobedient, and rebelled against thee, and cast thy law behind their backs, and slew thy prophets which testified against them to turn them to thee, and they wrought great provocations.* *Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because you build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous,* (Matthew 23:29) Nehemiah's confession puts two things side by side, that they *cast thy law behind their backs, and slew thy prophets*. The prophets came *to turn them to thee* and were killed for it, which is the history the builders of the tombs were standing on while saying they would have done differently.

cards.src_text: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because you build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous,
cards.tgt_text: Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit): as your fathers did, so do ye.
cards.note: Acts 7:51 — *Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit): as your fathers did, so do ye.* *Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because you build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous,* (Matthew 23:29) Stephen's line to the men in front of him is the woe in short, *as your fathers did, so do ye*. Like the ones decorating the tombs of the prophets, they honor the dead ones and *resist the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit)* in the living, which makes them heirs of the fathers they say they differ from.

cards.src_text: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because you build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous,
cards.tgt_text: But in the fourth generation they shall come hither again: for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full.
cards.old_note: *The iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full.* The measure-being-filled substance.
cards.note: Genesis 15:16 — *But in the fourth generation they shall come hither again: for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full.* *Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because you build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous,* (Matthew 23:29) Here the Torah shows judgment waiting on a measure: *the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full*, and for generations it held. The woe runs the same law from the other side, *Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers* (Matthew 23:32), the sins of the fathers carried on by those who build their tombs, until the measure is complete.

cards.src_text: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because you build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous,
cards.tgt_text: Is not this laid up in store with me, and sealed up among my treasures?
cards.old_note: *Is not this laid up in store with me?* The substance the Father-substance walks.
cards.note: Deuteronomy 32:34 — *Is not this laid up in store with me, and sealed up among my treasures?* *Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because you build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous,* (Matthew 23:29) Moses sings of a judgment that is not forgotten but *laid up in store*, sealed with Yahuah (the LORD), and a verse later says why it waits: *their foot shall slide in due time* (Deuteronomy 32:35). The blood of the prophets in the woe is that kind of stored account, held until the measure is full and then asked of the generation that fills it.

cards.src_text: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because you build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous,
cards.tgt_text: For ye, brethren, became followers of the churches of Elohim (God) which in Judaea are in HaMashiach Yahusha (Christ Jesus): for ye also have suffered like things of your own countrymen, even as they have of the Yahudim (Jews):
cards.old_note: *To fill up their sins alway.* The Pauline-restatement.
cards.note: 1 Thessalonians 2:14 — *For ye, brethren, became followers of the churches of Elohim (God) which in Judaea are in HaMashiach Yahusha (Christ Jesus): for ye also have suffered like things of your own countrymen, even as they have of the Yahudim (Jews):* *Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because you build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous,* (Matthew 23:29) Paul names the same pattern a generation on. The believers in Judæa suffered from men of their own people, and he says those who killed *their own prophets* (1 Thessalonians 2:15) did it *to fill up their sins alway* (1 Thessalonians 2:16). He is a Yahudi (Jew) writing about the men persecuting, and the assemblies in Judæa were Yahudim (Jews) too, so he describes the killers, not a people.

cards.src_text: You serpents, you generation of vipers, how can you escape the damnation of hell?
cards.tgt_text: But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees come to his baptism, he said unto them, O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come?
cards.note: Matthew 3:7 — *But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees come to his baptism, he said unto them, O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come?* *You serpents, you generation of vipers, how can you escape the damnation of hell?* (Matthew 23:33) John says *generation of vipers* to the *Pharisees and Sadducees* who came to his baptism, and Yahusha (Jesus) says it again to the scribes and Pharisees. Both times it falls on rulers who came with their standing, and both times it is joined to judgment, *the wrath to come* there and *the damnation of hell* here.

cards.src_text: You serpents, you generation of vipers, how can you escape the damnation of hell?
cards.tgt_text: O generation of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.
cards.note: Matthew 12:34 — *O generation of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.* *You serpents, you generation of vipers, how can you escape the damnation of hell?* (Matthew 23:33) He used the name before, with the reason attached: *how can ye, being evil, speak good things?* The words come out of what the heart is full of, and in this chapter he says what these men are full of, *within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity* (Matthew 23:28). The vipers are named by what comes out of them.

The vipers are named by what comes out of them.

cards.src_text: You serpents, you generation of vipers, how can you escape the damnation of hell?
cards.tgt_text: And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.
cards.note: Genesis 3:15 — *And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.* *You serpents, you generation of vipers, how can you escape the damnation of hell?* (Matthew 23:33) The serpent here has a seed, and *between thy seed and her seed* is the enmity set from the garden on. When Yahusha (Jesus) calls men on the seat *serpents*, he speaks of that seed surfacing inside the covenant people among the ones in the robes, and not of the people they were devouring, who are the sheep.

cards.src_text: You serpents, you generation of vipers, how can you escape the damnation of hell?
cards.tgt_text: Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it.
cards.old_note: *Ye are of your father the devil.*
cards.note: John 8:44 — *Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it.* *You serpents, you generation of vipers, how can you escape the damnation of hell?* (Matthew 23:33) Yahusha (Jesus) says it to men in front of him, *Ye are of your father the devil*, and then names the works, *a murderer from the beginning*. Matthew's *serpents* and John's children of the devil are one charge, made by what they do, as the woe goes on to say they will kill the prophets he sends. It is said of particular men, not of a people.

cards.src_text: Wherefore, behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: and some of them you shall kill and crucify; and some of them shall you scourge in your synagogues, and persecute them from city to city:
cards.tgt_text: And Cain talked with Abel his brother: and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.
cards.note: Genesis 4:8 — *And Cain talked with Abel his brother: and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.* *Wherefore, behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: and some of them you shall kill and crucify; and some of them shall you scourge in your synagogues, and persecute them from city to city:* (Matthew 23:34) He names where the count begins, *the blood of righteous Abel* (Matthew 23:35), and here is that blood being shed: Cain *rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him*. The sending of prophets and the killing of them start in the first field, and the woe says the whole count is coming due on the ones who keep it going.

cards.member_note: Genesis 4:8 — *Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.* Cain kills Abel his brother in the field, the first of the righteous blood Yahusha (Jesus) says is coming due on this generation.

cards.src_text: Wherefore, behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: and some of them you shall kill and crucify; and some of them shall you scourge in your synagogues, and persecute them from city to city:
cards.tgt_text: And the Spirit of Elohim (God) came upon Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest, which stood above the people, and said unto them, Thus saith Elohim (God), Why transgress ye the commandments of Yahuah (LORD), that ye cannot prosper? because ye have forsaken Yahuah (LORD), he hath also forsaken you.
cards.note: 2 Chronicles 24:20 — *And the Spirit of Elohim (God) came upon Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest, which stood above the people, and said unto them, Thus saith Elohim (God), Why transgress ye the commandments of Yahuah (LORD), that ye cannot prosper? because ye have forsaken Yahuah (LORD), he hath also forsaken you.* *Wherefore, behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: and some of them you shall kill and crucify; and some of them shall you scourge in your synagogues, and persecute them from city to city:* (Matthew 23:34) Matthew's Zechariah stands at the other end of the count, and this is the priest on whom the Spirit of Elohim (God) came, whose message was *Why transgress ye the commandments of Yahuah (LORD)*. The prophets were sent to press the commandments on a people who had left them, and that is what the sending and the killing both turn on.
cards.prose: Matthew's Zechariah stands at the other end of the count, and this is the priest on whom the Spirit of Elohim (God) came, whose message was *Why transgress ye the commandments of Yahuah (LORD)*. cards.member_note: 2 Chronicles 24:20 — *Thus saith Elohim (God), Why transgress ye the commandments of Yahuah (LORD), that ye cannot prosper?* The Spirit of Elohim (God) comes on Zechariah the priest to ask why they transgress the commandments of Yahuah (the LORD), and he is the slain prophet at the end of the count.

cards.src_text: Wherefore, behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: and some of them you shall kill and crucify; and some of them shall you scourge in your synagogues, and persecute them from city to city:
cards.tgt_text: In the eighth month, in the second year of Darius, came the word of Yahuah (LORD) unto Zechariah, the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo the prophet, saying,
cards.note: Zechariah 1:1 — *In the eighth month, in the second year of Darius, came the word of Yahuah (LORD) unto Zechariah, the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo the prophet, saying,* *Wherefore, behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: and some of them you shall kill and crucify; and some of them shall you scourge in your synagogues, and persecute them from city to city:* (Matthew 23:34) Matthew names *Zechariah son of Barachias* (Matthew 23:35), and here the writing prophet opens as *the son of Berechiah*, the same name in its Hebrew shape. Whether Yahusha (Jesus) means this Zechariah or the priest, Jehoiada's son, is left open on the page, and the point stands either way: the count of the slain reaches the temple and the altar.

The sender is the same voice that sent the prophets from the beginning, and the answer is the same, *some of them they shall slay and persecute*.

cards.src_text: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto you, how often would I have gathered your children together, even as a hen gathers her chickens under her wings, and you would not!
cards.tgt_text: As an eagle stirreth up her nest, fluttereth over her young, spreadeth abroad her wings, taketh them, beareth them on her wings:
cards.note: Deuteronomy 32:11 — *As an eagle stirreth up her nest, fluttereth over her young, spreadeth abroad her wings, taketh them, beareth them on her wings:* *O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto you, how often would I have gathered your children together, even as a hen gathers her chickens under her wings, and you would not!* (Matthew 23:37) Moses sings the same picture of Yahuah (the LORD) with an eagle's wings: *spreadeth abroad her wings, taketh them, beareth them on her wings*. Yahusha (Jesus) says he would have gathered the city's children *as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings*, so he stands where Moses placed Yahuah (the LORD) over the young. It is the one who carried them then who is speaking now.
