cards.src_text: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto you, how often would I have gathered your children together, even as a hen gathers her chickens under her wings, and you would not!
cards.tgt_text: Yahuah (LORD) recompense thy work, and a full reward be given thee of Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), under whose wings thou art come to trust.
cards.old_note: *Under whose wings thou art come to trust.*
cards.note: Ruth 2:12 — *Yahuah (LORD) recompense thy work, and a full reward be given thee of Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), under whose wings thou art come to trust.* *O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto you, how often would I have gathered your children together, even as a hen gathers her chickens under her wings, and you would not!* (Matthew 23:37) Boaz tells Ruth she has come *under whose wings thou art come to trust*, the wings of Yahuah (the LORD), the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel). Yahusha (Jesus) offers the same shelter to Jerusalem, gathering them *under her wings*, and says the refusal was theirs: *ye would not*.

cards.src_text: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto you, how often would I have gathered your children together, even as a hen gathers her chickens under her wings, and you would not!
cards.tgt_text: As birds flying, so will Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) defend Jerusalem; defending also he will deliver it; and passing over he will preserve it.
cards.old_note: *As birds flying, so will Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) defend Yerushalayim (Jerusalem).*
cards.note: Isaiah 31:5 — *As birds flying, so will Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) defend Jerusalem; defending also he will deliver it; and passing over he will preserve it.* *O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto you, how often would I have gathered your children together, even as a hen gathers her chickens under her wings, and you would not!* (Matthew 23:37) Isaiah's picture is a bird over its nest, *As birds flying*, and Yahusha (Jesus) uses the same image over the same city, wanting to gather her children under his wings. The one who promised to defend Jerusalem like that is now lamenting *ye would not*, so the desolation in the next verse reads as the defender stepping back.

cards.src_text: Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.
cards.tgt_text: I have forsaken mine house, I have left mine heritage; I have given the dearly beloved of my soul into the hand of her enemies.
cards.note: Jeremiah 12:7 — *I have forsaken mine house, I have left mine heritage; I have given the dearly beloved of my soul into the hand of her enemies.* *Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.* (Matthew 23:38) Yahuah (the LORD) speaks it in Jeremiah as grief, *I have forsaken mine house*, and while the house is given up, *the dearly beloved of my soul* is still named his own. Yahusha (Jesus) says the same at the temple, *your house is left unto you desolate*, and it is the house that is left, the temple and its rule, not the people he laments.

cards.src_text: Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.
cards.tgt_text: But if ye will not hear these words, I swear by myself, saith Yahuah (LORD), that this house shall become a desolation.
cards.note: Jeremiah 22:5 — *But if ye will not hear these words, I swear by myself, saith Yahuah (LORD), that this house shall become a desolation.* *Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.* (Matthew 23:38) The warning is conditional in Jeremiah: *if ye will not hear these words*, *this house shall become a desolation*. Yahusha (Jesus) says it now because the hearing was refused, and what is left desolate is the house, the building and the rule that sat in it.

cards.src_text: Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.
cards.tgt_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) went out, and departed from the temple: and his disciples came to him for to shew him the buildings of the temple.
cards.note: Matthew 24:1 — *And Yahusha (Jesus) went out, and departed from the temple: and his disciples came to him for to shew him the buildings of the temple.* *Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.* (Matthew 23:38) After *your house is left unto you desolate* the next thing Matthew tells is that he walks out: *departed from the temple*. The leaving is the saying acted out, and the disciples pointing at the buildings set up his answer, *There shall not be left here one stone upon another* (Matthew 24:2).

cards.src_text: Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.
cards.tgt_text: But when the king heard thereof, he was wroth: and he sent forth his armies, and destroyed those murderers, and burned up their city.
cards.note: Matthew 22:7 — *But when the king heard thereof, he was wroth: and he sent forth his armies, and destroyed those murderers, and burned up their city.* *Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.* (Matthew 23:38) The king of the parable answers the murder of his servants by burning *their city*. Yahusha (Jesus) says here that the house is left desolate to the men who kill the prophets he sends. The burned city and the desolate house are one judgment on the same rulers, told once in a story and once in plain speech.

cards.src_text: For I say unto you, You shall not see me henceforth, till you shall say, Blessed is he that comes in the name of Yahuah (Lord).
cards.tgt_text: Blessed be he that cometh in the name of Yahuah (LORD): we have blessed you out of the house of Yahuah (LORD).
cards.note: Psalm 118:26 — *Blessed be he that cometh in the name of Yahuah (LORD): we have blessed you out of the house of Yahuah (LORD).* *For I say unto you, You shall not see me henceforth, till you shall say, Blessed is he that comes in the name of Yahuah (Lord).* (Matthew 23:39) The parting word is a quotation. The line from the Psalm that the crowds sang at his coming, *Blessed be he that cometh in the name of Yahuah (LORD)*, is the line he says must be said again before he is seen. The leaving is not the end of it, since the same words are to come back from the same city.

cards.src_text: For I say unto you, You shall not see me henceforth, till you shall say, Blessed is he that comes in the name of Yahuah (Lord).

The multitudes before and behind *cried, saying, Hosanna to the Son of David*, and Yahusha (Jesus) says the city will not see him again until it says the blessing again. The cry was sung over him once at the gate, and the second time is the saying he waits for.

The men who will not say *Blessed is he that cometh* are the kind who objected when the children said it, and Yahusha (Jesus) says it will be said by them yet.

cards.src_text: For I say unto you, You shall not see me henceforth, till you shall say, Blessed is he that comes in the name of Yahuah (Lord).
cards.tgt_text: And I will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplications: and they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son, and shall be in bitterness for him, as one that is in bitterness for his firstborn.

cards.src_text: For I say unto you, You shall not see me henceforth, till you shall say, Blessed is he that comes in the name of Yahuah (Lord).
cards.tgt_text: And it shall come to pass, that in all the land, saith Yahuah (LORD), two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein.
cards.note: Zechariah 13:8 — *And it shall come to pass, that in all the land, saith Yahuah (LORD), two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein.* *For I say unto you, You shall not see me henceforth, till you shall say, Blessed is he that comes in the name of Yahuah (Lord).* (Matthew 23:39) The sorting runs ahead of the return. *Two parts therein shall be cut off and die*, and *the third shall be left therein*. The next verse says *I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined* (Zechariah 13:9), and that *they shall call on my name, and I will hear them* (Zechariah 13:9). So the saying of the blessing reads as coming from a refined third, not from the whole city.

cards.src_text: For I say unto you, You shall not see me henceforth, till you shall say, Blessed is he that comes in the name of Yahuah (Lord).
cards.tgt_text: For I would not, brethren, that ye should be ignorant of this mystery, lest ye should be wise in your own conceits; that blindness in part is happened to Yashar'el (Israel), until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in.
cards.note: Romans 11:25 — *For I would not, brethren, that ye should be ignorant of this mystery, lest ye should be wise in your own conceits; that blindness in part is happened to Yashar'el (Israel), until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in.* *For I say unto you, You shall not see me henceforth, till you shall say, Blessed is he that comes in the name of Yahuah (Lord).* (Matthew 23:39) Both run on an *until*. The house is left desolate for a time, and the end of it is a saving.

cards.src_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) went out, and departed from the temple: and his disciples came to him for to shew him the buildings of the temple.
cards.tgt_text: The word that came to Jeremiah from Yahuah (LORD), saying,
cards.note: Jeremiah 7:1 — *The word that came to Jeremiah from Yahuah (LORD), saying,* *And Yahusha (Jesus) went out, and departed from the temple: and his disciples came to him for to shew him the buildings of the temple.* (Matthew 24:1) The disciples show him the buildings, and this verse is where Yahuah (the LORD) sent a prophet to stand in the temple gate with the same news. Jeremiah's sermon says a house cannot shelter a people who trust it and will not amend their ways: *Trust ye not in lying words, saying, The temple of Yahuah (LORD), The temple of Yahuah (LORD), The temple of Yahuah (LORD), are these.* (Jeremiah 7:4)
cards.prose: The disciples show him the buildings, and this verse is where Yahuah (the LORD) sent a prophet to stand in the temple gate with the same news. Jeremiah's sermon says a house cannot shelter a people who trust it and will not amend their ways: *Trust ye not in lying words, saying, The temple of Yahuah (LORD), The temple of Yahuah (LORD), The temple of Yahuah (LORD), are these.* (Jeremiah 7:4)
cards.member_note: Jeremiah 7:1 — *The word that came to Jeremiah from Yahuah (LORD), saying,* Where Jeremiah's temple sermon begins, warning a people who trusted the house of Yahuah (the LORD) while they would not amend their ways.

cards.src_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) went out, and departed from the temple: and his disciples came to him for to shew him the buildings of the temple.
cards.tgt_text: Then will I make this house like Shiloh, and will make this city a curse to all the nations of the earth.
cards.note: Jeremiah 26:6 — *Then will I make this house like Shiloh, and will make this city a curse to all the nations of the earth.* *And Yahusha (Jesus) went out, and departed from the temple: and his disciples came to him for to shew him the buildings of the temple.* (Matthew 24:1) Yahusha (Jesus) says no stone will be left on another, and Jeremiah heard the same sentence long before: Yahuah (the LORD) will make the house *like Shiloh*. The reason stands in the verses just ahead of it, *If ye will not hearken to me, to walk in my law, which I have set before you* (Jeremiah 26:4), so the house falls for the law refused, not for the stones.
cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) says no stone will be left on another, and Jeremiah heard the same sentence long before: Yahuah (the LORD) will make the house *like Shiloh*. The reason stands in the verses just ahead of it, *If ye will not hearken to me, to walk in my law, which I have set before you* (Jeremiah 26:4), so the house falls for the law refused, not for the stones.
cards.member_note: Jeremiah 26:6 — *Then will I make this house like Shiloh, and will make this city a curse to all the nations of the earth.* The house made like Shiloh, said because the people would not hearken to walk in the law set before them.

cards.src_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) went out, and departed from the temple: and his disciples came to him for to shew him the buildings of the temple.
cards.tgt_text: Micah the Morasthite prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Yahudah (Judah), and spake to all the people of Yahudah (Judah), saying, Thus saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts); Zion shall be plowed like a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps, and the mountain of the house as the high places of a forest.
cards.note: Jeremiah 26:18 — *Micah the Morasthite prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Yahudah (Judah), and spake to all the people of Yahudah (Judah), saying, Thus saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts); Zion shall be plowed like a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps, and the mountain of the house as the high places of a forest.* *And Yahusha (Jesus) went out, and departed from the temple: and his disciples came to him for to shew him the buildings of the temple.* (Matthew 24:1) When Yahusha (Jesus) says the stones will be thrown down, he is saying what the elders in Jeremiah's day remembered Micah saying about Zion. They also remembered how it was met: *did he not fear Yahuah (LORD), and besought Yahuah (LORD), and Yahuah (LORD) repented him of the evil which he had pronounced against them?* (Jeremiah 26:19) The warning was always a call to turn as much as a sentence.

cards.src_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) went out, and departed from the temple: and his disciples came to him for to shew him the buildings of the temple.
cards.tgt_text: Therefore shall Zion for your sake be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps, and the mountain of the house as the high places of the forest.
cards.old_note: *Tsion (Zion) shall be plowed as a field.*
cards.note: Micah 3:12 — *Therefore shall Zion for your sake be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps, and the mountain of the house as the high places of the forest.* *And Yahusha (Jesus) went out, and departed from the temple: and his disciples came to him for to shew him the buildings of the temple.* (Matthew 24:1) Yahusha (Jesus) says the temple will be thrown down, and Micah says what made it ready to fall. The heads judged for reward, the priests taught for hire, the prophets divined for money, and every one of them said *Is not Yahuah (LORD) among us? none evil can come upon us.* (Micah 3:11) Zion is plowed *for your sake*, because of what its rulers made of it.

cards.src_text: For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Messiah (Christ); and shall deceive many.
cards.tgt_text: And I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians: and they shall fight every one against his brother, and every one against his neighbour; city against city, and kingdom against kingdom.
cards.note: Isaiah 19:2 — *And I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians: and they shall fight every one against his brother, and every one against his neighbour; city against city, and kingdom against kingdom.* *For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Messiah (Christ); and shall deceive many.* (Matthew 24:5) After those who come in his name, Yahusha (Jesus) says wars follow, *nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom* (Matthew 24:7). Isaiah already had that picture for Egypt and says whose hand it is: *I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians*, *city against city, and kingdom against kingdom*. What Matthew calls the beginning of sorrows is strife Yahuah (the LORD) can send among a people, not only a sign to watch for.

cards.note: Daniel 9:27 — *And he shall confirm the covenant with many for one week: and in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease, and for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate, even until the consummation, and that determined shall be poured upon the desolate.* *When you therefore shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, stand in the holy place, (whoso readeth, let him understand:)* (Matthew 24:15) Yahusha (Jesus) sends the reader to Daniel by name, so here is the verse itself. Daniel says the sacrifice and the oblation are made to cease in the midst of the week, and that *for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate*, until the end that is determined is poured out. Matthew's abomination is set to *stand in the holy place*, the place where that sacrifice was kept.

cards.src_text: When you therefore shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, stand in the holy place, (whoso readeth, let him understand:)
cards.tgt_text: And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people: and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book.
cards.old_note: *A time of trouble, such as never was.*
cards.note: Daniel 12:1 — *And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people: and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book.* *When you therefore shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, stand in the holy place, (whoso readeth, let him understand:)* (Matthew 24:15) A few verses on, Yahusha (Jesus) speaks of a tribulation with no equal, and Daniel gave that trouble its measure first: *a time of trouble*. In Daniel the trouble is not the last word. At that time *thy people shall be delivered*, and the ones named are those *found written in the book*.

cards.src_text: When you therefore shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, stand in the holy place, (whoso readeth, let him understand:)
cards.tgt_text: And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh.
cards.note: Luke 21:20 — *And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh.* *When you therefore shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, stand in the holy place, (whoso readeth, let him understand:)* (Matthew 24:15) Luke names what the desolation looks like when it arrives: *Jerusalem compassed with armies*. Where Matthew sends the reader to Daniel, Luke tells the disciples what they will see and what it means, *the desolation thereof is nigh*, and the same flight follows in both gospels, those in Judaea to the mountains.

cards.src_text: When you therefore shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, stand in the holy place, (whoso readeth, let him understand:)
cards.tgt_text: Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition;
cards.note: 2 Thessalonians 2:3 — *Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition;* *When you therefore shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, stand in the holy place, (whoso readeth, let him understand:)* (Matthew 24:15) Matthew has the abomination standing *in the holy place*, and Paul, one verse on, puts a man in the same kind of place: *so that he as Elohim (God) sitteth in the temple of Elohim (God), shewing himself that he is Elohim (God).* (2 Thessalonians 2:4) Both give the sign by where it stands, and Paul too begins by warning that none should be deceived before *a falling away* and the son of perdition.

cards.src_text: When you therefore shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, stand in the holy place, (whoso readeth, let him understand:)
cards.tgt_text: And there was given me a reed like unto a rod: and the angel stood, saying, Rise, and measure the temple of Elohim (God), and the altar, and them that worship therein.
cards.note: Revelation 11:1 — *And there was given me a reed like unto a rod: and the angel stood, saying, Rise, and measure the temple of Elohim (God), and the altar, and them that worship therein.* *When you therefore shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, stand in the holy place, (whoso readeth, let him understand:)* (Matthew 24:15) Matthew has the abomination standing in the holy place. Revelation counts that time in months; Matthew gives no count.

cards.src_text: When you therefore shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, stand in the holy place, (whoso readeth, let him understand:)
cards.tgt_text: And there was given unto him a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies; and power was given unto him to continue forty and two months.
cards.note: Revelation 13:5 — *And there was given unto him a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies; and power was given unto him to continue forty and two months.* *When you therefore shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, stand in the holy place, (whoso readeth, let him understand:)* (Matthew 24:15) Matthew gives the sign of the holy place and no number of months. Revelation shows *a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies*, given to the beast the dragon empowered, and *power was given unto him to continue forty and two months*. Revelation counts in months where Matthew counts nothing.

cards.src_text: Then if any man shall say unto you, Lo, here is Messiah (Christ), or there; believe it not.
cards.tgt_text: If there arise among you a prophet, or a dreamer of dreams, and giveth thee a sign or a wonder,
cards.note: Deuteronomy 13:1 — *If there arise among you a prophet, or a dreamer of dreams, and giveth thee a sign or a wonder,* *Then if any man shall say unto you, Lo, here is Messiah (Christ), or there; believe it not.* (Matthew 24:23) Yahusha (Jesus) warns that false prophets *shall shew great signs and wonders* (Matthew 24:24), and Moses had already given the test for such a sign. Even when *the sign or the wonder come to pass* (Deuteronomy 13:2), the prophet is refused if he leads away from Yahuah (the LORD), because the sign is the way Yahuah (the LORD) proves whether his people love him, and the standard is *keep his commandments, and obey his voice* (Deuteronomy 13:4).

cards.src_text: Then if any man shall say unto you, Lo, here is Messiah (Christ), or there; believe it not.
cards.tgt_text: Her young ones also suck up blood: and where the slain are, there is she.
cards.old_note: *Where the slain are, there is she.*
cards.note: Job 39:30 — *Her young ones also suck up blood: and where the slain are, there is she.* *Then if any man shall say unto you, Lo, here is Messiah (Christ), or there; believe it not.* (Matthew 24:23) Right after the warning against *Lo, here*, Yahusha (Jesus) says *wheresoever the carcase is, there will the eagles be gathered together* (Matthew 24:28). Job shows the bird: she dwells on the rock and *her eyes behold afar off* (Job 39:29), and *where the slain are, there is she*. Judgment needs no one to point to it; it finds the slain wherever they lie.

cards.src_text: Then if any man shall say unto you, Lo, here is Messiah (Christ), or there; believe it not.
cards.tgt_text: All ye beasts of the field, come to devour, yea, all ye beasts in the forest.
cards.old_note: *All ye beasts of the field, come to devour.*
cards.note: Isaiah 56:9 — *All ye beasts of the field, come to devour, yea, all ye beasts in the forest.* *Then if any man shall say unto you, Lo, here is Messiah (Christ), or there; believe it not.* (Matthew 24:23) Isaiah has the beasts called in to devour, and the verses after say why the flock is open: *they are shepherds that cannot understand: they all look to their own way, every one for his gain, from his quarter.* (Isaiah 56:11) Matthew has voices saying *Lo, here* and the eagles gathered to the carcase; Isaiah shows the carcase laid out by shepherds who looked to their own gain.

cards.tgt_text: Set the trumpet to thy mouth. He shall come as an eagle against the house of Yahuah (LORD), because they have transgressed my covenant, and trespassed against my law.

cards.src_text: Then if any man shall say unto you, Lo, here is Messiah (Christ), or there; believe it not.
cards.tgt_text: And they shall say to you, See here; or, see there: go not after them, nor follow them.

cards.note: Luke 17:23 — *And they shall say to you, See here; or, see there: go not after them, nor follow them.* *Then if any man shall say unto you, Lo, here is Messiah (Christ), or there; believe it not.* (Matthew 24:23) Luke puts the warning in the same order Matthew does. *See here; or, see there: go not after them* comes first, and then at once the lightning, *as the lightning, that lighteneth out of the one part under heaven, shineth unto the other part under heaven; so shall also the Son of Adam be in his day* (Luke 17:24). A coming that fills the sky cannot be pointed at in a room or a desert.

cards.src_text: Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken:
cards.tgt_text: For the stars of heaven and the constellations thereof shall not give their light: the sun shall be darkened in his going forth, and the moon shall not cause her light to shine.
cards.note: Isaiah 13:10 — *For the stars of heaven and the constellations thereof shall not give their light: the sun shall be darkened in his going forth, and the moon shall not cause her light to shine.* *Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken:* (Matthew 24:29) Isaiah says the stars *shall not give their light* and the sun is *darkened in his going forth*, and the verse before says whose day it is: *the day of Yahuah (LORD) cometh, cruel both with wrath and fierce anger, to lay the land desolate* (Isaiah 13:9). Yahusha (Jesus) uses the same darkened sun and moon for his coming, so the sky is the sign of the day of Yahuah (the LORD), and that day clears the sinners out of the land.

cards.src_text: Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken:
cards.tgt_text: Then the moon shall be confounded, and the sun ashamed, when Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) shall reign in mount Zion, and in Jerusalem, and before his ancients gloriously.
cards.note: Isaiah 24:23 — *Then the moon shall be confounded, and the sun ashamed, when Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) shall reign in mount Zion, and in Jerusalem, and before his ancients gloriously.* *Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken:* (Matthew 24:29) Matthew's moon gives no light and the sun is darkened; Isaiah says why they hide, *the moon shall be confounded, and the sun ashamed*, because Yahuah (the LORD) is reigning *in mount Zion, and in Jerusalem, and before his ancients gloriously*. The sky goes dark before a greater light, and the verse before has the host of the high ones and the kings of the earth shut up in the pit to be visited after many days.

cards.tgt_text: And all the host of heaven shall be dissolved, and the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll: and all their host shall fall down, as the leaf falleth off from the vine, and as a falling fig from the fig tree.
cards.old_note: *The heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll.*
cards.note: Isaiah 34:4 — *And all the host of heaven shall be dissolved, and the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll: and all their host shall fall down, as the leaf falleth off from the vine, and as a falling fig from the fig tree.* *Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken:* (Matthew 24:29) Matthew has the stars falling and the powers of the heavens shaken. cards.member_note: Joel 3:15 — *The sun and the moon shall be darkened, and the stars shall withdraw their shining.* Joel's darkened sun and moon fall in the valley of decision, where the harvest is ripe and Yahuah (the LORD) is the hope of his people.

cards.src_text: Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken:
cards.tgt_text: And when I shall put thee out, I will cover the heaven, and make the stars thereof dark; I will cover the sun with a cloud, and the moon shall not give her light.
cards.old_note: *I will cover the sun with a cloud.*
cards.note: Ezekiel 32:7 — *And when I shall put thee out, I will cover the heaven, and make the stars thereof dark; I will cover the sun with a cloud, and the moon shall not give her light.* *Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken:* (Matthew 24:29) Ezekiel's line is almost word for word Matthew's *the moon shall not give her light*, and it is spoken of the fall of Pharaoh, when Yahuah (the LORD) covers the heaven over him: *All the bright lights of heaven will I make dark over thee* (Ezekiel 32:8). The darkened sky is how the prophets speak when a proud power comes down, and Matthew sets it over the whole earth at his coming.

cards.member_note: Ezekiel 32:7 — *I will cover the heaven, and make the stars thereof dark; I will cover the sun with a cloud, and the moon shall not give her light.* Almost Matthew's words, said against Pharaoh when Yahuah (the LORD) puts him out: the sky is covered over a proud power's fall.

cards.src_text: Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken:
cards.tgt_text: And it shall come to pass in that day, saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD), that I will cause the sun to go down at noon, and I will darken the earth in the clear day:
cards.old_note: *I will cause the sun to go down at noon.*
cards.note: Amos 8:9 — *And it shall come to pass in that day, saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD), that I will cause the sun to go down at noon, and I will darken the earth in the clear day:* *Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken:* (Matthew 24:29) Amos has the sun going down at noon and Yahuah (the LORD) darkening the earth *in the clear day*. The verses after say what that day does to a people at ease: *I will turn your feasts into mourning, and all your songs into lamentation* (Amos 8:10), and then a famine, *not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of Yahuah (LORD)* (Amos 8:11). The darkness in the sky has a darkness in hearing to match.

cards.src_text: Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken:
cards.tgt_text: Therefore night shall be unto you, that ye shall not have a vision; and it shall be dark unto you, that ye shall not divine; and the sun shall go down over the prophets, and the day shall be dark over them.
cards.old_note: *The sun shall go down over the prophets.*
cards.note: Micah 3:6 — *Therefore night shall be unto you, that ye shall not have a vision; and it shall be dark unto you, that ye shall not divine; and the sun shall go down over the prophets, and the day shall be dark over them.* *Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken:* (Matthew 24:29) Micah turns the picture on the false prophets: night to them, no vision, *the day shall be dark over them*, and in the end *there is no answer of Elohim (God)* (Micah 3:7). The sun going down over them is a judgment on those who spoke for him falsely, and Matthew's darkened sun comes in a chapter that warns again and again of false prophets.

cards.member_note: Micah 3:6 — *the sun shall go down over the prophets, and the day shall be dark over them.* The sun goes down over the prophets who make his people err: no vision, no answer, the day dark over them.

cards.src_text: Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken:
cards.tgt_text: The great day of Yahuah (LORD) is near, it is near, and hasteth greatly, even the voice of the day of Yahuah (LORD): the mighty man shall cry there bitterly.
cards.note: Zephaniah 1:14 — *The great day of Yahuah (LORD) is near, it is near, and hasteth greatly, even the voice of the day of Yahuah (LORD): the mighty man shall cry there bitterly.* *Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken:* (Matthew 24:29) Zephaniah names the day the darkness belongs to: *The great day of Yahuah (LORD) is near*, and he describes it, *a day of darkness and gloominess, a day of clouds and thick darkness* (Zephaniah 1:15). Matthew puts the sun's darkening and the Son of Adam in the clouds in the same hour, and Zephaniah's day already has darkness and clouds in it.

cards.src_text: Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken:
cards.tgt_text: And I beheld when he had opened the sixth seal, and, lo, there was a great earthquake; and the sun became black as sackcloth of hair, and the moon became as blood;
cards.note: Revelation 6:12 — *And I beheld when he had opened the sixth seal, and, lo, there was a great earthquake; and the sun became black as sackcloth of hair, and the moon became as blood;* *Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken:* (Matthew 24:29) Revelation opens the sixth seal and shows the same sky: the sun goes black and the moon turns to blood, and then *the stars of heaven fell unto the earth, even as a fig tree casteth her untimely figs* (Revelation 6:13). Matthew's sun, moon and stars are the same three, told in this book's own words, with an earthquake and kings hiding in the rocks.

cards.src_text: Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken:
cards.tgt_text: And the fourth angel sounded, and the third part of the sun was smitten, and the third part of the moon, and the third part of the stars; so as the third part of them was darkened, and the day shone not for a third part of it, and the night likewise.
cards.note: Revelation 8:12 — *And the fourth angel sounded, and the third part of the sun was smitten, and the third part of the moon, and the third part of the stars; so as the third part of them was darkened, and the day shone not for a third part of it, and the night likewise.* *Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken:* (Matthew 24:29) Revelation has the darkening too, but by measure: at the fourth trumpet a third part of the sun, the moon and the stars is smitten, and day and night each lose a third. Matthew gives no fraction, and Revelation keeps its own count of trumpets; the next verse is an angel crying *Woe, woe, woe, to the inhabiters of the earth* (Revelation 8:13) for the trumpets still to sound.

cards.src_text: Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken:
cards.tgt_text: And I will shew wonders in heaven above, and signs in the earth beneath; blood, and fire, and vapour of smoke:
cards.note: Acts 2:19 — *And I will shew wonders in heaven above, and signs in the earth beneath; blood, and fire, and vapour of smoke:* *Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken:* (Matthew 24:29) Peter reads Joel to the men of Yashar'el (Israel) and keeps the sky signs in the reading: *The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before that great and notable day of Yahuah (Lord) come* (Acts 2:20). The darkened sun Matthew sets after the tribulation was already known to the apostles as what comes before the great day, a day still ahead of them.

cards.src_text: And then shall appear the sign of the Son of Adam in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of Adam coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
cards.tgt_text: I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.
cards.old_note: **Primary Tanakh-citation per Red Line #12.** *Like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven.*
cards.note: Daniel 7:13 — *I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.* *And then shall appear the sign of the Son of Adam in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of Adam coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.* (Matthew 24:30) Matthew has the Son of Adam coming on the clouds, and Daniel is the vision behind it: a figure *like* the Son of Adam, brought near before the Ancient of days. Daniel's word is *like*, for the one who comes took on flesh and looked like a son of Adam, and Daniel says what is given him: *dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all people, nations, and languages, should serve him* (Daniel 7:14). Yahusha (Jesus) takes that figure as himself.

cards.src_text: And then shall appear the sign of the Son of Adam in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of Adam coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
cards.tgt_text: And I will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplications: and they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son, and shall be in bitterness for him, as one that is in bitterness for his firstborn.
cards.old_note: *They shall look upon me whom they have pierced ... and the land shall mourn.*
cards.note: Zechariah 12:10 — *And I will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplications: and they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son, and shall be in bitterness for him, as one that is in bitterness for his firstborn.* *And then shall appear the sign of the Son of Adam in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of Adam coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.* (Matthew 24:30) Matthew has the tribes mourn when they see the Son of Adam coming. Zechariah says why: the house of David look on the one they pierced, and the mourning goes through the families one by one, *the land shall mourn, every family apart* (Zechariah 12:12). The one the tribes see in the clouds is the one they pierced.

Even so, Amen.* *And then shall appear the sign of the Son of Adam in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of Adam coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.* (Matthew 24:30) Revelation opens with the same sight in the same order: *he cometh with clouds; and every eye shall see him*, and then the mourning, *all kindreds of the earth shall wail because of him*, where Matthew has *all the tribes of the earth mourn*. John also names who is among those who see, *they also which pierced him*, and two verses on the speaker gives his own name: *which is, and which was, and which is to come* (Revelation 1:8).

cards.src_text: And then shall appear the sign of the Son of Adam in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of Adam coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
cards.tgt_text: And I looked, and behold a white cloud, and upon the cloud one sat like unto the Son of Adam, having on his head a golden crown, and in his hand a sharp sickle.
cards.old_note: The harvest-of-the-earth + *one sat like unto the Son of Adam* per Red Line #12.
cards.note: Revelation 14:14 — *And I looked, and behold a white cloud, and upon the cloud one sat like unto the Son of Adam, having on his head a golden crown, and in his hand a sharp sickle.* *And then shall appear the sign of the Son of Adam in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of Adam coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.* (Matthew 24:30) In Revelation the one on the cloud is seen *like unto the Son of Adam*, a golden crown on his head and *a sharp sickle* in his hand, and an angel comes out of the temple to cry *for the time is come for thee to reap; for the harvest of the earth is ripe* (Revelation 14:15). Matthew's Son of Adam on the clouds sends angels to gather; Revelation's rider holds the sickle himself, and the earth is reaped.

cards.src_text: And then shall appear the sign of the Son of Adam in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of Adam coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
cards.tgt_text: And I saw heaven opened, and behold a white horse; and he that sat upon him was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he doth judge and make war.
cards.note: Revelation 19:11 — *And I saw heaven opened, and behold a white horse; and he that sat upon him was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he doth judge and make war.* *And then shall appear the sign of the Son of Adam in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of Adam coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.* (Matthew 24:30) Revelation shows him coming another way: heaven opened, a white horse, a rider called *Faithful and True* who judges and makes war *in righteousness*, and whose name the next verses give as *The Word of Elohim (God)* (Revelation 19:13). Matthew's coming is in the clouds with a trumpet; this is another book's picture of his coming, a rider where Matthew has a cloud.

cards.src_text: And then shall appear the sign of the Son of Adam in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of Adam coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
cards.tgt_text: Who layeth the beams of his chambers in the waters: who maketh the clouds his chariot: who walketh upon the wings of the wind:
cards.note: Psalm 104:3 — *Who layeth the beams of his chambers in the waters: who maketh the clouds his chariot: who walketh upon the wings of the wind:* *And then shall appear the sign of the Son of Adam in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of Adam coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.* (Matthew 24:30) Matthew has the Son of Adam coming in the clouds, and the psalm says whose road the cloud is. Yahuah (the LORD) my Elohim (God) *maketh the clouds his chariot*, and *walketh upon the wings of the wind*. The one who rides the clouds in scripture is Yahuah (the LORD), and Yahusha (Jesus) puts his own coming there.

cards.tgt_text: Yahuah (LORD) is slow to anger, and great in power, and will not at all acquit the wicked: Yahuah (LORD) hath his way in the whirlwind and in the storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet.
cards.old_note: *Yahuah (the LORD) hath his way in the whirlwind.*
cards.note: Nahum 1:3 — *Yahuah (LORD) is slow to anger, and great in power, and will not at all acquit the wicked: Yahuah (LORD) hath his way in the whirlwind and in the storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet.* *And then shall appear the sign of the Son of Adam in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of Adam coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.* (Matthew 24:30) In Nahum the clouds are *the dust of his feet*, so the sky is only the road Yahuah (the LORD) walks. cards.src_text: And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.
cards.tgt_text: If any of thine be driven out unto the outmost parts of heaven, from thence will Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) gather thee, and from thence will he fetch thee:
cards.old_note: *Yahuah (the LORD) thy Elohim (God) gather thee from thence.*
cards.note: Deuteronomy 30:4 — *If any of thine be driven out unto the outmost parts of heaven, from thence will Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) gather thee, and from thence will he fetch thee:* *And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.* (Matthew 24:31) Moses told Yashar'el (Israel) that no one is too far to be fetched: even *the outmost parts of heaven* will not keep Yahuah (the LORD) from gathering his own. Matthew's *from one end of heaven to the other* is that reach, and the gathering follows the return, *shalt return unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), and shalt obey his voice according to all that I command thee this day* (Deuteronomy 30:2).

cards.src_text: And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.
cards.tgt_text: Behold, I will bring them from the north country, and gather them from the coasts of the earth, and with them the blind and the lame, the woman with child and her that travaileth with child together: a great company shall return thither.
cards.note: Jeremiah 31:8 — *Behold, I will bring them from the north country, and gather them from the coasts of the earth, and with them the blind and the lame, the woman with child and her that travaileth with child together: a great company shall return thither.* *And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.* (Matthew 24:31) Where Matthew sends angels to the four winds, Jeremiah sends the gathering first to the north country and then to *the coasts of the earth*, and the company that returns is not picked over: *the blind and the lame, the woman with child*, a great company. cards.tgt_text: And say unto them, Thus saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); Behold, I will take the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land:

cards.src_text: And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.
cards.tgt_text: And Yahuah (LORD) spake unto Moses, saying,
cards.old_note: The Yom Teru'ah (Feast of Trumpets) substance.
cards.note: Leviticus 23:23 — *And Yahuah (LORD) spake unto Moses, saying,* *And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.* (Matthew 24:31) The trumpet in Matthew has an old home in the appointed times. Yahuah (the LORD) told Moses that the first day of the seventh month is *a memorial of blowing of trumpets, an holy convocation* (Leviticus 23:24), a calling together of the assembly by trumpet. The great sound of a trumpet that gathers the elect in Matthew sounds the call the Torah already set for his people.

cards.src_text: And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.
cards.tgt_text: And in the seventh month, on the first day of the month, ye shall have an holy convocation; ye shall do no servile work: it is a day of blowing the trumpets unto you.

A convocation is a calling together, and Matthew's trumpet calls the elect together from every quarter; the day the Torah set aside for trumpets already carried that picture.

cards.src_text: And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.
cards.tgt_text: But I would not have you to be ignorant, brethren, concerning them which are asleep, that ye sorrow not, even as others which have no hope.
cards.old_note: *But I would not have you to be ignorant, brethren, concerning them which are asleep, that ye sorrow not, even as others which have no hope.* (1 Thessalonians 4:13). Paul's comfort concerning them which are asleep — not the same event as the Olivet gathering. The great trumpet of Matthew 24:31 gathers the scattered elect from the four winds at his return; the catching-up of 1 Thessalonians 4:17 comes after the reign and the little season.
cards.note: 1 Thessalonians 4:13 — *But I would not have you to be ignorant, brethren, concerning them which are asleep, that ye sorrow not, even as others which have no hope.* *And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.* (Matthew 24:31) Paul comforts those grieving *them which are asleep*: the hope is that *the dead in Messiah (Christ) shall rise first* (1 Thessalonians 4:16) at his coming, at the trump of Elohim (God), the same coming in which Matthew's great trumpet gathers the scattered elect. The catching up he names after it, *Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds* (1 Thessalonians 4:17), is a later thing, afterward, and the gathering of the elect is not it.

cards.src_text: And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.
cards.tgt_text: Behold, I shew you a mystery; We shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed,
cards.old_note: *Behold, I shew you a mystery; We shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed,* (1 Corinthians 15:51). The great sound of a trumpet that gathers the elect from the four winds sounds at his return; the change Paul names comes *at the last trump* (1 Corinthians 15:52), the seventh trumpet at the end, after the reign. Two trumpets of the one King, at the two edges of the reign.
cards.note: 1 Corinthians 15:51 — *Behold, I shew you a mystery; We shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed,* *And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.* (Matthew 24:31) Paul calls it a mystery that *we shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed*, and the verse after says when: *at the last trump: for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed* (1 Corinthians 15:52). Matthew has a great trumpet at his coming; Paul has the dead raised and the living changed at a trumpet.

cards.src_text: And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.
cards.tgt_text: And after these things I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth, that the wind should not blow on the earth, nor on the sea, nor on any tree.

The sealed are counted: *an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Revelation 7:4).

cards.src_text: And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.
cards.tgt_text: And I looked, and, lo, a Lamb stood on the mount Zion, and with him an hundred forty and four thousand, having his Father’s name written in their foreheads.
cards.note: Revelation 14:1 — *And I looked, and, lo, a Lamb stood on the mount Zion, and with him an hundred forty and four thousand, having his Father’s name written in their foreheads.* *And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.* (Matthew 24:31) The sealed of the tribes of Yashar'el (Israel) are seen again here with the Lamb on mount Zion, *having his Father's name written in their foreheads*, the seal they were given. cards.src_text: Now learn a parable of the fig tree; When his branch is yet tender, and puts forth leaves, you know that summer is nigh:
cards.tgt_text: For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled.
cards.old_note: *Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law.*
cards.note: Matthew 5:18 — *For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled.* *Now learn a parable of the fig tree; When his branch is yet tender, and puts forth leaves, you know that summer is nigh:* (Matthew 24:32) The fig tree tells the season, and the verse after it says what outlasts the season: *Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.* (Matthew 24:35) He measured his words the same way on the mountain where he taught, heaven and earth going before *one jot or one tittle* goes from the law. The words that will not pass are the law's own, so nothing in the Olivet talk reads as the commandments ending.

cards.src_text: Now learn a parable of the fig tree; When his branch is yet tender, and puts forth leaves, you know that summer is nigh:
cards.tgt_text: Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away.
cards.note: Mark 13:31 — *Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away.* *Now learn a parable of the fig tree; When his branch is yet tender, and puts forth leaves, you know that summer is nigh:* (Matthew 24:32) Mark gives the fig tree the same close, with his words outlasting heaven and earth, and runs it straight into the hidden hour: *But of that day and that hour knoweth no man* (Mark 13:32). The sign you can read in the leaves and the day nobody can name sit side by side, with his words standing over both.

cards.src_text: Now learn a parable of the fig tree; When his branch is yet tender, and puts forth leaves, you know that summer is nigh:
cards.tgt_text: Of old hast thou laid the foundation of the earth: and the heavens are the work of thy hands.
cards.old_note: *They shall perish, but thou shalt endure.*
cards.note: Psalm 102:25 — *Of old hast thou laid the foundation of the earth: and the heavens are the work of thy hands.* *Now learn a parable of the fig tree; When his branch is yet tender, and puts forth leaves, you know that summer is nigh:* (Matthew 24:32) The psalm says of the heavens and earth what Matthew says: they are made things and they pass. *They shall perish, but thou shalt endure: yea, all of them shall wax old like a garment* (Psalm 102:26). The one addressed laid the foundation of the earth *of old*, and when Yahusha (Jesus) sets his words against the passing of heaven and earth, he puts them on the side of what endures.

cards.src_text: Now learn a parable of the fig tree; When his branch is yet tender, and puts forth leaves, you know that summer is nigh:
cards.tgt_text: The grass withereth, the flower fadeth: but the word of our Elohim (God) shall stand for ever.

cards.tgt_text: Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look upon the earth beneath: for the heavens shall vanish away like smoke, and the earth shall wax old like a garment, and they that dwell therein shall die in like manner: but my salvation shall be for ever, and my righteousness shall not be abolished.
cards.old_note: *The heavens shall vanish away ... but my salvation shall be for ever.*
cards.note: Isaiah 51:6 — *Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look upon the earth beneath: for the heavens shall vanish away like smoke, and the earth shall wax old like a garment, and they that dwell therein shall die in like manner: but my salvation shall be for ever, and my righteousness shall not be abolished.* *Now learn a parable of the fig tree; When his branch is yet tender, and puts forth leaves, you know that summer is nigh:* (Matthew 24:32) Isaiah sets the passing of heaven and earth against what does not pass: the heavens *vanish away like smoke*, the earth *wax old like a garment*, but *my righteousness shall not be abolished*. The verse after says who is listening, *the people in whose heart is my law* (Isaiah 51:7), so what is not abolished is tied to the law in the heart.

The verse after says who is listening, *the people in whose heart is my law* (Isaiah 51:7), so what is not abolished is tied to the law in the heart.

cards.src_text: But of that day and hour knows no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only.
cards.tgt_text: And he saith unto them, Ye shall drink indeed of my cup, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with: but to sit on my right hand, and on my left, is not mine to give, but it shall be given to them for whom it is prepared of my Father.
cards.old_note: *Not mine to give, but ... of my Father.* The Son's-eternal-submission per the Formless-Formed grid.
cards.note: Matthew 20:23 — *And he saith unto them, Ye shall drink indeed of my cup, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with: but to sit on my right hand, and on my left, is not mine to give, but it shall be given to them for whom it is prepared of my Father.* *But of that day and hour knows no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only.* (Matthew 24:36) Twice in Matthew the one who is Elohim (God) points past himself to the Father. At the cup the seats at his right and left are not his to give but the Father's to prepare, and here the day and hour are known to the Father only. He does not lose what he is by saying so; the Son stands under the Father and says it plainly.
cards.prose: Twice in Matthew the one who is Elohim (God) points past himself to the Father. At the cup the seats at his right and left are not his to give but the Father's to prepare, and here the day and hour are known to the Father only. He does not lose what he is by saying so; the Son stands under the Father and says it plainly.
cards.member_note: Matthew 20:23 — *to sit on my right hand, and on my left, is not mine to give, but it shall be given to them for whom it is prepared of my Father.* The seats at his right and left are not his to give but the Father's, the same deference he shows about the day and hour.

cards.src_text: But of that day and hour knows no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only.
cards.tgt_text: But of that day and that hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels which are in heaven, neither the Son, but the Father.
cards.note: Mark 13:32 — *But of that day and that hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels which are in heaven, neither the Son, but the Father.* *But of that day and hour knows no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only.* (Matthew 24:36) Mark names the Son himself among those who do not know the day: not man, not the angels, *neither the Son, but the Father*. Matthew's *but my Father only* says the same from the other side. The Son who is Elohim (God) stands under the Father's timing and says so.
cards.prose: Mark names the Son himself among those who do not know the day: not man, not the angels, *neither the Son, but the Father*. Matthew's *but my Father only* says the same from the other side. The Son who is Elohim (God) stands under the Father's timing and says so.
cards.member_note: Mark 13:32 — *But of that day and that hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels which are in heaven, neither the Son, but the Father.* Mark adds that neither the Son knows the day and hour, but the Father only, the parallel to Matthew 24:36.

cards.src_text: But of that day and hour knows no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only.
cards.tgt_text: When they therefore were come together, they asked of him, saying, Adonai (Lord), wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Yashar'el (Israel)?
cards.old_note: *It is not for you to know the times or the seasons, which the Father hath put in his own power.*
cards.note: Acts 1:6 — *When they therefore were come together, they asked of him, saying, Adonai (Lord), wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Yashar'el (Israel)?* *But of that day and hour knows no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only.* (Matthew 24:36) After the resurrection the disciples ask the question they asked on the mount in its plainest form: *restore again the kingdom to Yashar'el (Israel)?* He does not say there will be no restoring. He says the times are *which the Father hath put in his own power* (Acts 1:7), and Matthew's *my Father only* is the same answer.

cards.src_text: But of that day and hour knows no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only.
cards.tgt_text: Yahuah (LORD) said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.
cards.note: Psalm 110:1 — *Yahuah (LORD) said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.* *But of that day and hour knows no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only.* (Matthew 24:36) Matthew shows the Son holding the day back to the Father; the psalm shows the same order in a picture. David's *my Lord* sits at the right hand of Yahuah (the LORD) *until* the Father makes his enemies the footstool, so the one at the right hand waits on the Father for the day.

cards.src_text: But as the days of Noah were, so shall also the coming of the Son of Adam be.
cards.tgt_text: And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born unto them,
cards.old_note: The substantial-pre-flood-substance + the Watcher-Rebellion-substance per Red Line #11.
cards.note: Genesis 6:1 — *And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born unto them,* *But as the days of Noah were, so shall also the coming of the Son of Adam be.* (Matthew 24:37) Matthew names marrying and giving in marriage as the mark of the days of Noah, and Genesis shows what marriage had become: *the sons of Elohim (God) saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.* (Genesis 6:2) The days Yahusha (Jesus) points to began with that crossing, so the days of Noah are more than eating and drinking.

cards.member_note: Genesis 6:1 — *And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born unto them,* The days of Noah begin when men multiply and the sons of Elohim (God) take the daughters of men as wives.

cards.src_text: But as the days of Noah were, so shall also the coming of the Son of Adam be.
cards.tgt_text: And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Noah, Come thou and all thy house into the ark; for thee have I seen righteous before me in this generation.
cards.note: Genesis 7:1 — *And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Noah, Come thou and all thy house into the ark; for thee have I seen righteous before me in this generation.* *But as the days of Noah were, so shall also the coming of the Son of Adam be.* (Matthew 24:37) Matthew has Noah going into the ark and the rest knowing nothing until the flood took them. Genesis gives Noah's side: Yahuah (the LORD) calls him and his house in because *thee have I seen righteous before me in this generation*. One household was called in while the world went on eating and marrying, and the flood that *took them all away* (Matthew 24:39) was judgment on the rest.

cards.src_text: But as the days of Noah were, so shall also the coming of the Son of Adam be.
cards.tgt_text: And spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly;
cards.old_note: *Spared not the old world, but saved Noach (Noah) the eighth person.*
cards.note: 2 Peter 2:5 — *And spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly;* *But as the days of Noah were, so shall also the coming of the Son of Adam be.* (Matthew 24:37) Peter sets Noah beside the angels that sinned: Elohim (God) *spared not the angels that sinned* (2 Peter 2:4) and *spared not the old world*, bringing the flood on the ungodly, and saved Noah as *a preacher of righteousness*. In Matthew the people ate and married and knew nothing, while the preacher was building the ark.

cards.src_text: But as the days of Noah were, so shall also the coming of the Son of Adam be.
cards.tgt_text: Knowing this first, that there shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts,
cards.note: 2 Peter 3:3 — *Knowing this first, that there shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts,* *But as the days of Noah were, so shall also the coming of the Son of Adam be.* (Matthew 24:37) Matthew says they *knew not until the flood came* (Matthew 24:39), and Peter says the scoffers of the last days walk after their own lusts and ask *Where is the promise of his coming?* (2 Peter 3:4), since all things go on as they were. He answers from the flood: *the world that then was, being overflowed with water, perished* (2 Peter 3:6). Those who say nothing will change are Noah's world over again.

cards.src_text: But as the days of Noah were, so shall also the coming of the Son of Adam be.
cards.tgt_text: And as it was in the days of Noah, so shall it be also in the days of the Son of Adam.
cards.note: Luke 17:26 — *And as it was in the days of Noah, so shall it be also in the days of the Son of Adam.* *But as the days of Noah were, so shall also the coming of the Son of Adam be.* (Matthew 24:37) Luke has the same saying and carries the picture further: *They did eat, they drank, they married wives, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noah entered into the ark, and the flood came, and destroyed them all.* (Luke 17:27) Then comes Lot, and *the same day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven* (Luke 17:29). Flood and fire both take the unwatching, and in both the household is brought out first.

cards.src_text: Then shall two be in the field; the one shall be taken, and the other left.
cards.tgt_text: I tell you, in that night there shall be two men in one bed; the one shall be taken, and the other shall be left.
cards.note: Luke 17:34 — *I tell you, in that night there shall be two men in one bed; the one shall be taken, and the other shall be left.* *Then shall two be in the field; the one shall be taken, and the other left.* (Matthew 24:40) In Luke the disciples ask where, and the answer is not a rescue: *Wheresoever the body is, thither will the eagles be gathered together.* (Luke 17:37) So the ones taken in Luke are taken to where the carcase lies, which agrees with Matthew, where the flood *took them all away* (Matthew 24:39) and then *the one shall be taken, and the other left*.

cards.src_text: Then shall two be in the field; the one shall be taken, and the other left.
cards.tgt_text: Let both grow together until the harvest: and in the time of harvest I will say to the reapers, Gather ye together first the tares, and bind them in bundles to burn them: but gather the wheat into my barn.
cards.old_note: The wheat-and-tares post-harvest-sifting substance per Red Line #11.
cards.note: Matthew 13:30 — *Let both grow together until the harvest: and in the time of harvest I will say to the reapers, Gather ye together first the tares, and bind them in bundles to burn them: but gather the wheat into my barn.* *Then shall two be in the field; the one shall be taken, and the other left.* (Matthew 24:40) The order is the text's: *first the tares*, bound and burned, and then the wheat gathered into the barn. So *the one shall be taken, and the other left* cannot be the righteous lifted away and the wicked left behind. In Noah's day those taken were the ones the flood took away; the tares go first, and the wheat is gathered after.

cards.src_text: Then shall two be in the field; the one shall be taken, and the other left.
cards.tgt_text: The Son of Adam shall send forth his angels, and they shall gather out of his kingdom all things that offend, and them which do iniquity;
cards.old_note: The wheat-and-tares post-harvest-sifting substance per Red Line #11.
cards.note: Matthew 13:41 — *The Son of Adam shall send forth his angels, and they shall gather out of his kingdom all things that offend, and them which do iniquity;* *Then shall two be in the field; the one shall be taken, and the other left.* (Matthew 24:40) Here the Son of Adam sends his angels, as in Matthew 24, and what they gather first is *all things that offend, and them which do iniquity*. Iniquity is lawlessness again. The ones taken in the field and at the mill are such as these, gathered out by the angels, and the ones left are still in the field when the tares are gone.

cards.src_text: Then shall two be in the field; the one shall be taken, and the other left.
cards.tgt_text: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a net, that was cast into the sea, and gathered of every kind:
cards.note: Matthew 13:47 — *Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a net, that was cast into the sea, and gathered of every kind:* *Then shall two be in the field; the one shall be taken, and the other left.* (Matthew 24:40) The net is the same lesson: it *gathered of every kind*, and the sorting comes at the shore, where *the angels shall come forth, and sever the wicked from among the just* (Matthew 13:49). The two in the field and the two at the mill are such a sorting, and the wicked are the ones taken out from among the just, not the just lifted out of the world.

cards.src_text: Watch therefore: for you know not what hour your Lord does come.
cards.tgt_text: But of the times and the seasons, brethren, ye have no need that I write unto you.
cards.old_note: The day-of-Yahuah-substance + *as a thief in the night*.
cards.note: 1 Thessalonians 5:1 — *But of the times and the seasons, brethren, ye have no need that I write unto you.* *Watch therefore: for you know not what hour your Lord does come.* (Matthew 24:42) Matthew says *ye know not what hour*; Paul says he does not need to write about *the times and the seasons*, because *yourselves know perfectly that the day of Yahuah (Lord) so cometh as a thief in the night* (1 Thessalonians 5:2). It falls on those who say *Peace and safety* (1 Thessalonians 5:3), but *ye, brethren, are not in darkness, that that day should overtake you as a thief* (1 Thessalonians 5:4).
cards.prose: Matthew says *ye know not what hour*; Paul says he does not need to write about *the times and the seasons*, because *yourselves know perfectly that the day of Yahuah (Lord) so cometh as a thief in the night* (1 Thessalonians 5:2). It falls on those who say *Peace and safety* (1 Thessalonians 5:3), but *ye, brethren, are not in darkness, that that day should overtake you as a thief* (1 Thessalonians 5:4).
cards.member_note: 1 Thessalonians 5:1 — *But of the times and the seasons, brethren, ye have no need that I write unto you.* Paul says the times and seasons need no writing, for the day comes as a thief, and the verses after tell who it overtakes.

cards.src_text: Watch therefore: for you know not what hour your Lord does come.
cards.tgt_text: Remember therefore how thou hast received and heard, and hold fast, and repent. If therefore thou shalt not watch, I will come on thee as a thief, and thou shalt not know what hour I will come upon thee.
cards.old_note: *If therefore thou shalt not watch, I will come on thee as a thief.*
cards.note: Revelation 3:3 — *Remember therefore how thou hast received and heard, and hold fast, and repent. If therefore thou shalt not watch, I will come on thee as a thief, and thou shalt not know what hour I will come upon thee.* *Watch therefore: for you know not what hour your Lord does come.* (Matthew 24:42) Revelation puts the thief in his own mouth, to the assembly in Sardis, who had *a name that thou livest, and art dead* (Revelation 3:1). The reason for the watching is given: *hold fast, and repent*, or he comes as a thief and they will not know the hour. Even there he finds *a few names even in Sardis which have not defiled their garments* (Revelation 3:4).

If therefore thou shalt not watch, I will come on thee as a thief, and thou shalt not know what hour I will come upon thee.* He warns Sardis to watch or he will come as a thief, and notes a few names there who have not defiled their garments.

cards.src_text: Watch therefore: for you know not what hour your Lord does come.
cards.tgt_text: Behold, I come as a thief. Blessed is he that watcheth, and keepeth his garments, lest he walk naked, and they see his shame.
cards.note: Revelation 16:15 — *Behold, I come as a thief. Blessed is he that watcheth, and keepeth his garments, lest he walk naked, and they see his shame.* *Watch therefore: for you know not what hour your Lord does come.* (Matthew 24:42) The thief saying is dropped into the middle of the gathering for battle, *the battle of that great day of El Shaddai (God Almighty)* (Revelation 16:14), and the blessing is on *he that watcheth, and keepeth his garments*. Matthew's household that watches is Revelation's man who keeps his garments, and the one who does not stands naked with his shame seen.

cards.src_text: Watch therefore: for you know not what hour your Lord does come.
cards.tgt_text: But the day of Yahuah (Lord) will come as a thief in the night; in the which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat, the earth also and the works that are therein shall be burned up.
cards.old_note: *The day of Yahuah (the LORD) will come as a thief in the night.*
cards.note: 2 Peter 3:10 — *But the day of Yahuah (Lord) will come as a thief in the night; in the which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat, the earth also and the works that are therein shall be burned up.* *Watch therefore: for you know not what hour your Lord does come.* (Matthew 24:42) Peter gives the thief the full weight of the day: *as a thief in the night*, and what is in it burns. The verse before explains the delay: *Yahuah (Lord) is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness* (2 Peter 3:9). The master's delay is not neglect, and the evil servant in Matthew who says it will not come is counting wrongly.

cards.src_text: Who then is a faithful and wise servant, whom his lord has made ruler over his household, to give them meat in due season?
cards.tgt_text: For the kingdom of heaven is as a man travelling into a far country, who called his own servants, and delivered unto them his goods.
cards.note: Matthew 25:14 — *For the kingdom of heaven is as a man travelling into a far country, who called his own servants, and delivered unto them his goods.* *Who then is a faithful and wise servant, whom his lord has made ruler over his household, to give them meat in due season?* (Matthew 24:45) The next parable opens the same way as the faithful servant's: a master goes away and puts his goods into his servants' hands. In Matthew 24 the goods are the household's meat in due season; in Matthew 25 they are talents. Both ask what each servant did with what was delivered to him while the master was gone.
cards.prose: The next parable opens the same way as the faithful servant's: a master goes away and puts his goods into his servants' hands. In Matthew 24 the goods are the household's meat in due season; in Matthew 25 they are talents. Both ask what each servant did with what was delivered to him while the master was gone.
cards.member_note: Matthew 25:14 — *For the kingdom of heaven is as a man travelling into a far country, who called his own servants, and delivered unto them his goods.* The same stewardship in the next scene: a man travels, delivers his goods to his servants, and the question is what each did with them.

cards.src_text: Who then is a faithful and wise servant, whom his lord has made ruler over his household, to give them meat in due season?
cards.tgt_text: And Yahusha (Lord) said, Who then is that faithful and wise steward, whom his lord shall make ruler over his household, to give them their portion of meat in due season?
cards.note: Luke 12:42 — *And Yahusha (Lord) said, Who then is that faithful and wise steward, whom his lord shall make ruler over his household, to give them their portion of meat in due season?* *Who then is a faithful and wise servant, whom his lord has made ruler over his household, to give them meat in due season?* (Matthew 24:45) Luke puts the same servant after the thief and the hour *when ye think not* (Luke 12:40), and has Peter ask whether the parable is for the twelve or for all. Yahusha (Jesus) answers with the steward set over a household. Matthew's *faithful and wise servant* is Luke's *faithful and wise steward*, the one given the household's portion in season.

In chapter 21 the husbandmen are the rulers of the house, and they killed the servants sent for the fruit; in this chapter the servant over the household is tested the same way, by whether he feeds it or *begin to smite his fellowservants* (Matthew 24:49).

threads.title: The third telling on the road up to Jerusalem
threads.summary_md:
It ain't new. On the road up to Jerusalem Yahusha (Jesus) takes the twelve apart and tells them a third time what waits at the end of it.
